Electronic referrals were abstracted from the medical record and nonparametric tests were used for comparisons. Thirty-six intervention and 32 control patients were included in the analysis. Child demographic and clinical characteristics were balanced. Overall, 26.5% of children had severely uncontrolled chronic asthma. Referrals upon ED discharge were significantly greater for the intervention group (63.9% versus 6.3% in the control group, P <0.0001). Referrals were more frequently provided for patients with uncontrolled asthma (n = 18) than for patients with controlled asthma (n = 7). Most referrals were to a subspecialty clinic (28.0%) or a community asthma program (68.0%). There was a ten-fold increase in referrals provided to children with asthma at the time of ED discharge with use of the PACCI-ED. Most referrals were for children with poorly controlled asthma who were referred to subspecialty asthma care.

articles.title: Modified starch powder versus epinephrine gauze for hemostasis during burn wound debridement: A randomized intra-patient trial.
articles.journal: Burns : journal of the International Society for Burn Injuries
articles.abstract: Severe intraoperative hemorrhage during burn wound debridement is a major challenge. Topical hemostatics help rapidly control bleeding, but agents must be effective, safe, and easy to use. This study compared a modified starch powder with standard epinephrine-saturated gauze for hemorrhage control during burn wound debridement. A prospective, randomized, intra-patient-controlled trial was conducted with 30 patients undergoing burn debridement. For each patient, two comparable wound sites were randomized to receive starch powder (AriClot) or epinephrine-saturated gauze. The primary outcomes were time to hemostasis and bleeding flow rate. Secondary outcomes included surgeon satisfaction, early graft loss, ischemia, and wound infection. Statistical analysis was performed using appropriate paired tests. The starch powder-treated sites had a significantly shorter time to hemostasis (median 1.5 min vs. 5 min; p < 0.001) and a significantly lower bleeding flow rate than the control sites (median 3 ml/min/TBSA% vs. 7 ml/min/TBSA%; p < 0.001). Surgeon satisfaction was notably higher with starch powder, with 76.67% of applications rated as "Perfect" compared with 10% for the control treatment (p < 0.001). Wound site infection was significantly lower with starch powder (p = 0.027). There were no statistically significant differences in graft rejection (p = 0.275) or ischemia (p = 0.220) between the two intervention sites. Carboxymethyl starch-based hemostatic agent improved hemostasis compared with epinephrine-saturated gauze during burn wound debridement. Its use was associated with faster hemostasis and higher surgeon satisfaction, without increasing the risk of adverse wound outcomes. IRCT20180609040016N6 (https://irct.behdasht.gov.ir/trial/78594).

articles.title: Shock wave therapy versus conventional physical therapy for partial-thickness forearm burn scars: A randomized controlled trial.
articles.journal: Burns : journal of the International Society for Burn Injuries
articles.abstract: Burn scars are the lasting marks left on the skin following a burn injury, which can arise from exposure to heat, chemicals, electricity, or radiation. Burn scars can have both physical and psychological impacts, affecting mobility, sensitivity, and self-esteem. To explore and compare the efficacy of shock wave therapy (SWT) vs. conventional physical therapy in the treatment of partial-thickness forearm burn scars. Double-blind, randomized controlled trial (RCT). Seventy patients aged 20-55 with partial-thickness forearm burns were allocated into two groups: Group A (35 participants) got SWT, whereas Group B (35 participants) had traditional physical therapy with a deactivated applicator. Ultrasonography assessment, the Vancouver Scar Scale, and the Burn Specific Health Scale-Brief (BSHS-B) were evaluated at baseline, after 8 weeks (post intervention), and following an additional 8-week period of follow-up. Treatments Consisted of 24 sessions, each lasting 45 min, and conducted three times per week. No notable changes were detected between groups at baseline assessment. Both groups exhibited statistically significant enhancements across all outcome measures (VAS, thickness, VSS, and BSHS) from pre to post and pre to follow-up, as evidenced by the 95% confidence intervals (CIs) that do not intersect zero in any comparison. Group A consistently had shorter and elevated confidence intervals (CIs); for instance, the VAS pre-post CI was (4.70, 6.36) in Group A compared to (4.19, 6.86) in Group B, and the BSHS pre-post CI was (26.23, 106.66) in Group A vs (28.07, 105.23) in Group B. Furthermore, Group A exhibited significant enhancement in VAS (η²p = 0.82 and 0.80), VSS (η²p = 0.80 and 0.79), and BSHS (η²p = 0.85 for both pre-post and pre-follow-up), signifying a considerable intervention impact. SWT has been demonstrated to be effective in improving the properties of scar tissue, particularly by alleviating pain and enhancing the appearance of hypertrophic scars.

articles.title: PermeaDerm accelerates early wound healing in partial-thickness burns: A multicenter randomized controlled trial.
articles.journal: Burns : journal of the International Society for Burn Injuries
articles.abstract: This multicenter, randomized controlled trial evaluated the safety and efficacy of PermeaDerm, a biosynthetic wound matrix, compared to porcine acellular dermal matrix (ADM) for the treatment of partial-thickness burns in Chinese patients. A total of 184 patients were enrolled and randomized 1:1 to receive either PermeaDerm or ADM across the four Chinese centers. The primary endpoint was the proportion of wounds that achieved complete re-epithelialization by day 14 (superficial partial-thickness burns) or 21 (deep partial-thickness burns). The secondary endpoints included complete re-epithelialization over time, wound area reduction rate (cm2/day), time to complete re-epithelialization, pain scores, device performance, and incidence of complications. PermeaDerm was non-inferior to ADM for the primary endpoint. On day 7, significantly more wounds treated with PermeaDerm achieved early complete re-epithelialization for superficial partial-thickness burns (55.6% [20/36] vs. 27.0% [10/37], p = 0.012) and deep partial-thickness burns (37.2% [19/51] vs. 12.7% [7/55], p = 0.005). The median wound area reduction rate at day 7 was also significantly higher with PermeaDerm for both superficial partial-thickness burns (2.41 cm²/day (IQR 0.86-5.07) vs. 1.05 cm²/day (IQR 0.34-3.01), p = 0.034) and deep partial-thickness burns (3.50 cm²/day (IQR 1.40-8.02) vs. 1.78 cm²/day (IQR 0.85-4.40), p = 0.021). After day 7, the healing rates were comparable between the groups. Median time to complete re-epithelialization was 3 days shorter with PermeaDerm for both superficial (7.00 days (IQR 6-10.25) vs. 10.00 days (IQR 7-12.75), p = 0.016) and deep partial-thickness burns (10.00 days (IQR 7-13) vs. 13.00 days (IQR 10-15), p = 0.003). Pain scores and complication rates were similar between the groups, while PermeaDerm was associated with more favorable ease of application, wound visibility, and removal. PermeaDerm accelerates early wound healing and shortens the time to complete re-epithelialization compared with ADM, while maintaining a comparable safety profile. These findings suggest that PermeaDerm may represent a clinically useful alternative for the management of partial-thickness burns.

articles.title: Enhancing High-Fidelity Simulation Flight-Based Training for Critical Care Paramedics in EMS Aviation: A Systematic Review.
articles.abstract: High-fidelity simulation (HFS) is used with critical care paramedics (CCPs) to enhance preparedness in high-stake scenarios. This systematic review aims to assess the evidence on the role and effectiveness of HFS flight-based training, evaluating its application in education for CCPs operating within emergency medical services aviation settings. A systematic literature search was performed using a set of inclusion and exclusion criteria, resulting in 7 articles which were appraised using the Critical Appraisal Skills Programme tool. HFS training equips learners with skills relevant to their practice. CCPs register improved expertise, engagement and motivation, responsiveness, and general mood. There was insufficient evidence on whether this modality enhances self-awareness. HFS learning is feasible in training CCPs in emergency medical services aviation. However, there is limited evidence on the performance of CCPs trained using HFS learning in the prehospital setting. The findings suggest that standardizing training and assessment methods is recommended to optimize skill acquisition, improve team performance, and enhance patient safety in high-acuity emergencies.

articles.title: Youth Suicide Prevention Is Core Emergency Care.
Is a Minute Saved More Than a Minute Earned? Ambient Scribes and the Work Behind the Note.
Metabolic Failure and EEG Abnormalities After Cardiac Arrest: Which Comes First, the Chicken or the Egg?
Trends in Care and Outcomes Among Emergency Department Patients With Chest Pain Without Myocardial Infarction.
articles.abstract: To characterize trends in hospitalization, downstream care, and outcomes among emergency department (ED) patients with chest pain without acute myocardial infarction (AMI) diagnosis. We analyzed claims data from a large national commercial insurer (2007-2021) and identified ED visits with a principal diagnosis of chest pain. We excluded visits with secondary diagnoses of AMI or other significant cardiopulmonary conditions and those preceded by cardiac testing, coronary procedures, AMI admissions, or chest pain ED visits within 6 months. Usage outcomes included index hospitalization (principal), 7-day cardiac testing, and 30-day coronary revascularization. The principal clinical outcome was 180-day postindex AMI hospitalization. Adjusted annual rates were estimated using generalized estimating equations, and trends were assessed using inverse-variance-weighted linear regression. We included 773,250 index chest pain ED visits (mean age 54.2 years; 54.3% women). Adjusted hospitalization rates declined from 42.7% to 18.6%, and 7-day noninvasive testing decreased from 26.7% to 9.1%. Revascularization within 30 days declined from 5.8% to 3.6%. Overall, 180-day postindex AMI hospitalization showed no significant temporal trend, ranging from 0.8% to 1.2%. However, a modest increasing trend was observed among patients aged 70 years and older. Among ED patients with chest pain without AMI diagnosis, hospitalization, cardiac testing, and revascularization declined substantially from 2007 to 2021. Overall, downstream AMI hospitalization remained stable, although those in older adults experienced modest rises. Although efforts continue to identify additional low-risk patients for safe discharge, future research should quantify the potential benefits of hospitalization and cardiac testing, particularly for older adults and high-risk patients.

articles.title: Concepts in Practice: Understanding and Addressing Name-Based Microaggressions in Health Care.
articles.abstract: Names are important markers of identity, culture, and belonging. In health care settings, individuals with ethnically distinct names may experience repeated mispronunciations, unsolicited nicknames, or avoidance of their names. Repeated mispronunciations without sincere efforts to learn or improve, as well as the avoidance, dismissal, or replacement of names with unsolicited nicknames, may function as name-based microaggressions and can negatively affect psychological safety, professional identity formation, and workplace inclusion. In this manuscript, we discuss the effect of name-based microaggressions on health care professionals and trainees, with particular focus on the emergency department. We review the 3 major categories of microaggressions-microassaults, microinsults, and microinvalidations-and use clinical vignettes to demonstrate how these behaviors may appear in both interpersonal and institutional settings. We also propose practical interpersonal and institutional strategies to promote more inclusive workplaces and foster respectful engagement with ethnically distinct names. By encouraging greater awareness, curiosity, humility, and intentionality around names, health care organizations can help cultivate clinical environments where individuals feel respected, included, and valued.

articles.title: A High-Yield Solution to the Emergency Medicine Resident Scholarly Activity Requirement.
Live Versus Delayed Video-Based TEAM Assessment During Real-World Cardiac Arrest: Agreement and Exploratory Differences by Rater Experience.
articles.abstract: To evaluate agreement between immediate live and delayed video-based assessment of nontechnical skills during real-world adult cardiac arrest resuscitation, and whether agreement differed by rater experience. We conducted a prospective observational study of adult cardiac arrest resuscitations in a tertiary emergency department in Taiwan in 2024. For each event, one trained physician or nurse who participated in the resuscitation completed the Team Emergency Assessment Measure (TEAM) immediately afterward and re-rated the same event from video approximately 30 days later. Live-video agreement was assessed using intraclass correlation coefficients and Bland-Altman analysis. Of 105 recorded resuscitations, 80 had complete paired assessments. Mean global ratings were similar between modalities (8.25 versus 8.22; mean paired difference, -0.03; 95% confidence interval [CI] -0.25 to 0.20), whereas teamwork scores were modestly lower on video review (mean paired difference, -1.00; 95% CI -1.77 to -0.23). Event-level agreement was limited: intraclass correlation coefficients were 0.21 (95% CI 0.00 to 0.41) for total TEAM score and 0.16 (95% CI -0.06 to 0.37) for global rating. Total TEAM video ratings averaged 1.24 points lower than live ratings, with limits of agreement from -12.28 to 9.80. Agreement was higher among senior raters. Delayed video-based TEAM assessment produced similar group-level scores but limited event-level agreement during real-world cardiac arrest. Agreement appeared higher among senior raters. Video review may support debriefing and monitoring, but appraisal of a specific resuscitation or other higher stakes use likely requires experienced raters and structured safeguards.

articles.title: Controlling time-related biases in ECPR observational studies.
Efficacy and Safety of Ulinastatin in the Treatment of Patients with Sepsis: The ADJUST Trial.
articles.abstract: Urinary trypsin inhibitor (ulinastatin, UTI) has shown potential survival benefits in sepsis; however, conclusive clinical evidence is lacking. In patients with sepsis, does adjunctive ulinastatin, compared with placebo, reduce 28-day all-cause mortality? In this multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial, adult ICU patients with sepsis meeting Sepsis-3 criteria within 48 hours of admission were randomized (1:1) to receive intravenous UTI (400,000 IU every 8 hours) or placebo, for up to 10 days in addition to standard care. Randomization was stratified by site and septic shock. The primary endpoint was 28-day all-cause mortality. Secondary endpoints included ICU, hospital, and 90-day mortality, and ICU/hospital length of stay. Of 347 patients randomized, 340 (169 UTI, 171 placebo) received intervention and were included in the safety analysis; after 5 post-intervention withdrawals, 335 (165 UTI, 170 placebo) were included in the intention-to-treat analysis. At 28 days, death had occurred in 39 of 165 patients (23.6%) in the UTI group and in 39 of 170 patients (22.9%) in the placebo group (absolute difference, 0.7% [95% CI -8.4% to 9.7%]; P = .98; hazard ratio 1.03, 95% CI 0.66 to 1.61, P = .90). Secondary outcomes were similar in the two groups. Adverse events occurred in 56.8% (96/169) of UTI and 42.7% (73/171) of placebo patients (absolute difference 14.1%, 95% CI 3.6%-24.6%; P = 0.009). In patients with sepsis, adjunctive UTI did not reduce mortality compared with placebo. Routine use of UTI for sepsis is not supported by these findings. ClinicalTrials.gov; https://clinicaltrials.gov; NCT02647554.

articles.title: Transfer of prehospital defibrillator recordings to receiving hospitals after out-of-hospital cardiac arrest: a 16-year retrospective study in Paris.
Calculating trauma undertriage rates: Are we using the wrong formula-and the wrong definition?
articles.journal: The journal of trauma and acute care surgery
articles.abstract: Undertriage (UT) is central to trauma center quality improvement, yet UT definitions vary, and no data-driven consensus target exists for interfacility benchmarking. We compared facility-level UT rates across four methods and assessed the impact on facility benchmarking. This retrospective study included patients aged 18 to 89 from Level I & II trauma centers in the ACS TQP Files (2021-2023). Facility-level UT was calculated using the Cribari Matrix Method (CMM), modified Cribari Matrix Method (mCMM), Standardized Triage Assessment Tool (STAT), and High-Intensity Time-Sensitive (HITS) intervention-based definition representing trauma team actions. Paired facility-level UT rates were compared across methods. To estimate benchmarking impact, we calculated within-facility rank change (higher rank = higher UT) relative to CMM. 2,643,881 patients and 515 facilities were included. Median facility-level UT significantly differed by method: CMM 11% [interquartile range: 9-14], mCMM 60% [50-67], STAT 6% [5-8], and HITS 30% [22-40] (all P<0.001). At individual hospitals, the median range of maximum UT values between methods was 53% [44-60]. The median absolute facility rank change between the CMM method and other tools was 129 [54.5-236.5] for mCMM, 48 [17-90] for STAT, and 142 [62.5-252.5] for HITS. These UT data highlight a concerning level of variation and uncertainty in the calculation and interpretation of a key trauma center performance metric. Until a UT definition is standardized and data-driven UT target goals established, cross-center benchmarking using UT should be interpreted cautiously and may be better suited for within-center trending. Level III, therapeutic/care management.

articles.title: Vasopressors as immunomodulators: a hidden axis in septic shock.
The Impact of Undernutrition on Post-Tuberculosis Lung-Function: A Prospective Cohort Study.
articles.abstract: Undernutrition is the leading driver of tuberculosis worldwide, yet its effect on the lungs of people who complete treatment is not well defined. Among adults treated for drug-sensitive pulmonary tuberculosis, is undernutrition associated with worse post-treatment lung function, radiographic severity, exercise capacity and respiratory quality of life, and does systemic inflammation mediate that association? Adults (≥18 years) with drug-sensitive pulmonary tuberculosis were enrolled at treatment initiation in India. We measured associations of baseline body mass index (BMI), mid-upper arm circumference (MUAC), and premorbid BMI with spirometry, chest radiograph score, six-minute walk distance and St George's Respiratory Questionnaire score. Plasma IFN-γ, TNF-α and IL-6 were measured at baseline and month 2; counterfactual mediation analysis partitioned the effect of undernutrition on lung function into direct and inflammation-mediated components. Of 156 participants analyzed, 76 (48.7%) had a ventilatory defect; 52 (33.3%) had airflow obstruction and 31 (19.9%) had restrictive spirometry. Each 1 kg/m2 higher baseline BMI was associated with lower odds of any ventilatory defect (adjusted odds ratio [aOR], 0.78; 95% CI, 0.67-0.90), and BMI below 16 kg/m2 carried five-fold higher odds than BMI ≥18.5 kg/m2 (aOR, 5.08; 95% CI, 1.76-16.02). MUAC and premorbid BMI showed similar associations. Lower BMI was associated with restrictive spirometry (aOR, 0.74 per kg/m2; 95% CI, 0.59-0.89) but not airflow obstruction (aOR, 0.91; 95% CI, 0.80-1.03). Undernourished participants had higher baseline IL-6, which mediated 32% (FEV1) and 49% (FVC) of the association with impaired lung function. Undernutrition before and at treatment initiation is a potentially modifiable determinant of post-treatment lung impairment, with systemic inflammation mediating part of the effect. Nutritional assessment belongs in routine tuberculosis care, and nutritional support should be tested to prevent lung-function impairment in tuberculosis survivors.

articles.title: The impact of removing prior authorization for guideline-concordant maintenance inhaled medications for COPD: a population-based cohort study.
articles.abstract: Most patients with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) do not receive maintenance inhaled therapies in concordance with evidence-based clinical guidelines. Long-acting muscarinic antagonists (LAMA), the recommended first-line therapy, is underused, while inhaled corticosteroids (ICS)/long-acting beta-agonists (LABA) are often used in discordance with clinical guidelines. In July 2020, British Columbia's (BC) universal drug plan removed prior authorization requirements for coverage for LAMA medications and restricted coverage for ICS/LABA. What is the impact of this policy change on guideline-concordant maintenance inhaled medication use? In a population-based cohort study using provincial administrative health data, we identified patients with COPD using a validated case definition and followed them from January 2019 (18 months pre-policy) to December 2022 (30 months post-policy). Using interrupted time series analysis, we evaluated the monthly proportion of patients filling a prescription for ICS/LABA and LAMA, mean canisters dispensed, proportion of days covered (PDC), rates of ICS/LABA discontinuation, LAMA (re)initiation, and initiating LAMA as first maintenance therapy. We report absolute differences between observed and counterfactual outcomes at study end. The cohort included 47,583 patients with COPD (mean 71.5 years, 46.5% female, 31.7 months mean follow-up). Thirty months post-policy change, ICS/LABA use decreased by -1.3% (95% CI -2.4, -0.3) and LAMA use increased by 0.8% (95% CI 0.1, 1.6). There was no significant change in the number of ICS/LABA canisters dispensed, PDC or proportion discontinuing ICS/LABA. Mean LAMA canisters dispensed increased by 9.8 per 1,000 patients (95% CI 1.0, 18.7) and PDC increased by 1.5% (95% CI 0.5, 2.4). (Re)initiation of LAMA or initiating LAMA as maintenance therapy increased by 0.2% (95% CI 0.02, 0.3) and 34.8% (95% CI 22.3, 48.6), respectively. Total combined drug costs did not change. Changes to drug coverage in BC were associated with improved guideline-concordant medication use.

articles.title: Pretransplant Pulmonary Hemodynamics, Explant Histology, and Primary Graft Dysfunction after Lung Transplantation for Silicosis.
articles.abstract: Silicosis associated with progressive massive fibrosis (PMF) is a major cause of end-stage lung disease among workers in the artificial stone industry. Patients with PMF are increasingly referred for lung transplant (LTx) evaluation and there is emerging evidence of pulmonary hypertension (PH) in patients with advanced PMF. Among patients with PMF referred for lung transplantation, what is the incidence of PH and what are accompanying histopathologic pulmonary vascular aberrations? Retrospective single-center cohort study of prospectively-enrolled participants, providing granular data on the invasive hemodynamic profile of patients with silicosis-associated PMF, histopathologic data on pulmonary vascular aberrations, and clinical data on post-transplant complications. Clinical and sociodemographic variables were collected. Explanted lungs from patients with silicosis-associated PMF underwent detailed pulmonary vascular histopathologic review and were descriptively compared with PAH explants. The incidence of primary graft dysfunction (PGD) was evaluated and descriptive analysis performed to provide associations of clinical features and PGD incidence. PH was present in over 95% of 21 patients with silicosis-associated PMF who underwent LTx, with a hemodynamic profile similar to patients transplanted for PAH. . Silicosis explants showed confluent silicotic nodules, extensive fibrosis and hyalinization, obscuration or obliteration of vascular structures, and perivascular fibrohistiocytic infiltrates with extrinsic narrowing. Classic PAH-type arteriolar muscular hypertrophy and plexiform arteriopathy were uncommon. In exploratory comparisons, patients who developed PGD had more frequent pretransplant right ventricular dysfunction (71% vs 21%; risk difference 0.50, 95% CI 0.06-0.75) and a lower median TAPSE/RVSP ratio (0.27 vs 0.39; Hedges' g -0.93, 95% CI -1.88 to 0.02) than in those without PGD. These findings suggest that PH in advanced silicosis with PMF is very common and represents a distinct pulmonary vascular phenotype characterized by extensive fibrotic vascular obliteration rather than the classic arteriopathy seen in PAH.

articles.title: Evaluating AI Chatbots for Real-Time Detection of Incorrect Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation Positioning.
Calcium in trauma resuscitation: Transfusion volume or measurement-guided replacement?
articles.journal: The journal of trauma and acute care surgery

articles.title: PIEZO1 activation alters membrane remodeling and aggregability of stored red blood cells.
articles.journal: The journal of trauma and acute care surgery
articles.abstract: Transfused red blood cells (RBCs) actively contribute to post-injury hemostasis due to surface phosphatidylserine (PS) exposure. We hypothesized that storage sensitizes erythrocytes to the PIEZO1-induced, calcium‑dependent, PS externalization through calcium and protein kinase C (PKC) dependent activation of the phospholipid scramblase TMEM16F. Five units of type O whole blood were obtained for analysis at days 21 and 42 of storage. RBC PS was quantified by annexin V staining on flow cytometry at increasing extracellular CaCl₂ concentrations (0, 0.5, 1.0, 2.0, and 5.0 mmol/L), with and without the PIEZO1 agonist Yoda1 (0.2 μM), PKC agonist Phorbol 12-myristate 13-acetate (PMA; 6 μM) and antagonist chelerythrine chloride (CC; 10 μM), and the TMEM16 family inhibitor niclosamide (2 μM). RBC aggregometry was assessed by multiplate. Data were analyzed by analysis of variance and mixed-effects modeling. PS exposure increased in a Ca²⁺‑dependent manner in both day 21 and 42 RBCs (p<0.001). PIEZO1 stimulation enhanced this response to a greater extent in day 42 RBCs, with greater change in PS at 1 mmol/L (2.21% vs. -0.44%, p=0.021), 2 mmol/L (7.36% vs. 0.53%, p<0.001), and 5 mmol/L (12.09% vs. 6.40%, p<0.001) CaCl2. Compared with calcium alone, Yoda1 and PMA (+61.3%, p<0.001 for both) produced similar increases in PS externalization, whereas PKC inhibition (-45.6%, p=0.009) and TMEM16F inhibition (-4.6%, p=0.99) negated the PIEZO1 response. Yoda1 agonism preserved RBC aggregability after 42 days of storage (51.2±39.0 vs. 2.0±3.5 area under the curve, p<0.001). Storage sensitizes RBCs to PIEZO1-mediated, calcium-dependent, PS externalization through PKC- and TMEM16F-dependent signaling. Given its endogenous mechanosensitive properties, pharmacologic PIEZO1 activation highlights a potential mechanism by which mechanical stress encountered during trauma and transfusion through the injured microcirculation may promote erythrocyte phospholipid membrane remodeling and aggregability, contributing to the procoagulant activity of transfused RBCs.

articles.title: Long-Term Mortality in Sepsis Survivors: A Population-Based Study During 15 Years.
articles.abstract: To evaluate long-term mortality among sepsis survivors in Catalonia over a 15-year period and to identify factors associated with increased mortality within 2 years after hospital discharge. Retrospective population-based cohort study. Acute-care hospitals in Catalonia, Spain. Adult and pediatric patients hospitalized with sepsis between 2005 and 2019 identified using the International Classification of Diseases, 9th Revision, Clinical Modification and International Classification of Diseases, 10th Revision, Clinical Modification codes for infection and acute organ dysfunction. Patients who died during hospitalization, were transferred to another facility, or represented readmission episodes were excluded. None. Data were obtained from the Catalan Minimum Basic Dataset of Acute-Care Hospitals, with longitudinal follow-up through the Central Registry of Insured Persons. Comorbidities were assessed using the Charlson comorbidity index. Logistic regression and Cox proportional hazards models were used to identify predictors of long-term mortality. Among 296,554 hospital admissions for sepsis, 237,075 patients (79.9%) survived to hospital discharge. Of these, 42% died (99,571) within 2 years. Long-term mortality increased significantly with age, ranging from 5.8% in patients younger than 15 years to 62% in those older than 84 years (p < 0.0001), and with comorbidity burden (21%, 38%, 51%, and 67% for Charlson index 0, 1-2, 3-4, and ≥ 5, respectively; p < 0.0001). Neoplasia (hazard ratio [HR], 2.011), liver cirrhosis (HR, 1.562), and dementia (HR, 1.304) were the comorbidities most strongly associated with mortality. Longer hospital stays were also associated with increased mortality. A progressive decline in long-term mortality was observed during 2017-2019. Long-term mortality among sepsis survivors remains high, with more than 40% dying within 2 years after hospital discharge. These findings support the need for structured post-sepsis care strategies focused on high-risk patients, improved continuity of care, and prevention of long-term sepsis-related complications.

articles.title: Persistent gaps in health-related quality of life measures for older adult trauma patients: A systematic review.
articles.journal: The journal of trauma and acute care surgery
articles.abstract: Older adults experience persistent functional and psychosocial consequences after trauma, but it remains unclear whether commonly used health-related quality of life (HRQoL) instruments adequately measure recovery in this population. This systematic review appraised psychometric evidence and risk of bias for HRQoL instruments used in United States trauma cohorts that included adults aged 65 years or older. MEDLINE, EMBASE, and CINAHL were searched from inception through January 28, 2026. Two reviewers independently screened studies and extracted data. Risk of bias was evaluated using an adapted Risk of Bias in Non-randomized Studies-of Interventions (ROBINS-I) assessment. Studies evaluating an HRQoL instrument as the target measure underwent Consensus-based Standards for the Selection of Health Measurement Instruments (COSMIN) Risk of Bias assessment for each reported measurement property. Results were rated as sufficient, insufficient, or indeterminate and synthesized by instrument. Of 17,195 records, 19 studies were included. Studies most often examined isolated orthopedic trauma (n=7, 36.8%), spinal cord injury (n=6, 31.6%), other injury populations (n=3, 15.8%), polytrauma or systemic injury (n=2, 10.5%), and burns (n=1, 5.3%). Frequently evaluated domains included physical functioning (n=16), emotional or mental health (n=13), overall life satisfaction (n=13), social functioning (n=11), and physical symptoms (n=10). Although all studies used at least one previously developed patient-reported measure, none explicitly adapted or comprehensively validated an eligible HRQoL instrument for older adult trauma patients. Ten studies evaluated a target HRQoL instrument, contributing 33 COSMIN measurement property assessments: 19 sufficient, 10 indeterminate, and 4 insufficient. Overall risk of bias was low in six studies, moderate in eight, serious in three, and unclear in two. Existing studies show that HRQoL instruments have been used in trauma cohorts including older adults, but they do not establish validity for older adult trauma patients specifically. Future studies should evaluate promising instruments in cohorts designed around older adults' recovery priorities and clinical characteristics after trauma. Systematic Review; Level III.

articles.title: Shortening the Family Satisfaction in the ICU (FS-ICU): Development and Validation of a 12-Item Family Satisfaction Survey for Adult ICUs.
articles.abstract: To develop and validate a shorter Family Satisfaction in the ICU (FS-ICU) questionnaire that reduces survey length while preserving content and psychometric performance for quality improvement and benchmarking. The FS-ICU survey assesses family perceptions of care, communication, and decision-making and has been translated into multiple languages with implementation across diverse health care systems internationally. In a province-wide electronic implementation in Ontario, more than 40% of initiated surveys were incomplete, suggesting that survey length may limit practicality for large-scale quality improvement and benchmarking. Multistage study using provincial FS-ICU survey data and an independent multicenter validation dataset for item reduction, psychometric evaluation, agreement testing, and external validation of a shortened questionnaire. A 12-member expert working group, convened for a Critical Care Services Ontario initiative, used provincial web-based data from adult ICUs across Ontario to develop a shorter version, FS-ICUshort. External validation was applied to FS-ICUshort using a separate multicenter Canadian revised FS-ICU dataset. A 12-member expert working group led by Dr. Daren K. Heyland, including administrative staff, ICU clinical staff, patient experience specialists, and quality improvement specialists from Ontario, used provincial FS-ICU rollout data. None. Using empirical criteria and expert ratings, the FS-ICU was reduced from 29 to 12 items: seven in the satisfaction-with-care domain (FS-Care) and five in the communication and decision-making domain (FS-DM). FS-ICUshort showed high internal consistency (Cronbach's α = 0.93 for FS-Care, 0.86 for FS-DM, and 0.94 for total). Confirmatory factor analysis supported a two-factor structure with better fit than a single-factor model. Scores from FS-ICUshort closely matched full FS-ICU, with mean differences less than or equal to 1.1 points on a 0-100 scale and intraclass correlations of 0.97-0.99. External validation replicated these results. The 12-item FS-ICUshort maintains the core content and psychometric quality of the original FS-ICU while significantly reducing length, supporting routine use in ICU family experience measurement and benchmarking.

articles.title: Consensus on a core outcome set for ventilation trials in critically ill patients with acute brain injury: results of an international Delphi consensus study.
articles.abstract: Clinical research evaluating mechanical ventilation liberation in patients with acute brain injury (ABI) shows substantial outcome heterogeneity, limiting evidence synthesis. We aimed to develop an internationally endorsed core outcome set (COS) and a hierarchical composite endpoint for ventilation trials in neurocritical care. Following COS-STAD/COS-STAP standards, we conducted a 4-round international Delphi study. Candidate outcomes were identified via a scoping review. A multidisciplinary panel from 31 countries scored outcomes using a 9-point GRADE scale. Inclusion required >70% rating as "critical" (score 7-9) and ≤15% as "not important" (1-3). Two consensus meetings were held to categorize outcomes, select representative measures, and ratify a hierarchical composite endpoint. 78 stakeholders participated in Round 1; 60 completed all rounds (23.1% attrition). Fifty-four outcomes achieved Delphi consensus. At Consensus Meeting 1, these were organized into 16 categories; the highest-scoring outcome per category was selected. Three outcomes were not ratified due to disease-specificity (NIH Stroke Scale) or lack of universal applicability (brain death, coma-free days). The final COS comprised 13 outcomes across 5 domains: respiratory function, survival, complications, functional status, and quality of life. A 3-level hierarchical composite endpoint was ratified at Consensus Meeting 2: (1) intensive care unit survival, (2) no reintubation within 72 hours, and (3) days alive without mechanical ventilation. This study establishes the first COS for ventilation weaning trials in ABI patients. Widespread adoption of these 13 outcomes and the hierarchical composite endpoint will standardize reporting, enable meaningful evidence synthesis, and facilitate clinical translation in neurocritical care. Core Outcome Measures in Effectiveness Trials (COMET) Initiative, registration number 2320.

Network Trauma Research series: Modeling Trauma Complexity: Rodent Platforms for Studying Bone Healing and Hemorrhagic Shock.
articles.abstract: Polytrauma, defined as severe injury to multiple body regions often accompanied by physiological instability, remains a major global health burden with high morbidity and mortality. Among the most clinically relevant two-injury combinations, long-bone fractures and hemorrhagic shock are particularly important, as both critically influence systemic inflammation, remote organ dysfunction such as lung or kidney damage, and tissue regeneration itself. To improve translational understanding of these complex interactions, robust small-animal models, particularly murine systems, have been developed to experimentally dissect the biological mechanisms underlying fracture healing, hypovolemic shock, and their combined effects. This review provides a comprehensive overview of current rodent models for isolated fracture, hemorrhagic shock, and combination trauma. Key methodological variables, such as fracture induction methods, fixation strategies, hemorrhage protocols, anesthesia and analgesia, and the influence of age, sex, and comorbidities are outlined to support informed model selection. Additionally, this manuscript highlights the challenges and opportunities in designing clinically relevant "double-hit" models that mimic real-world trauma patterns while maintaining high reproducibility and animal welfare standards. Collectively, the summarized evidence underscores the importance of standardized, physiologically meaningful preclinical trauma models to advance mechanistic insights and foster the development of effective therapeutic interventions.

articles.title: Dynamic phenotyping and organ cross-talk in sepsis-associated organ injury: from physiological trajectories to precision critical care.
articles.abstract: Sepsis-associated organ injury remains a major cause of mortality in critically ill patients. Conventional assessment relies largely on physiological indicators, including lactate, mean arterial pressure (MAP), PaO2/FiO2 ratio, creatinine, urine output, and organ dysfunction scores. However, these isolated values or single-variable trends may incompletely capture the temporal instability and biological heterogeneity that characterize sepsis. Increasing evidence indicates that dynamic trajectories, variability patterns, and evolving subphenotypes may better characterize disease progression, organ recovery, and treatment responsiveness. In parallel, critical care medicine is moving from syndrome-level classification toward treatable traits, individualized treatment effects, and precision critical care. Dynamic phenotyping focuses on physiological trajectories, including lactate clearance, oxygenation evolution, hemodynamic variability, glycemic variability, and renal recovery, but its major value may lie in interpreting relationships among trajectories across organ systems. Interpretation of dynamic phenotypes therefore requires attention to cross-system temporal relationships, including coordinated recovery, coupled deterioration, and discordant recovery. From this trajectory-based perspective, sepsis-associated organ injury can be viewed as an interconnected multiorgan network involving lung-kidney, gut-lung, gut-liver, gut-kidney, and endothelial-organ cross-talk. Organ cross-talk may help explain dynamic coupling among organ systems, whereas microcirculatory-mitochondrial dysfunction may contribute to trajectory mismatch through impaired tissue perfusion, oxygen delivery-utilization uncoupling, bioenergetic failure, maladaptive metabolic reprogramming, and defective mitochondrial quality control. This trajectory-based perspective may inform future precision critical care, while most trajectory-guided strategies remain investigational and require prospective validation before routine clinical adoption.

articles.title: Hospital variation in emergency admission rates from English emergency departments.
Brachial-to-Radial Arterial Pressure Gradient: Implications for Clinical Practice.
Network Trauma Research Series: Modeling Trauma Complexity - In Vitro Models to Study Traumatic Lung Damage.
articles.abstract: Polytrauma, defined as severe injury to multiple body regions, frequently affects the head and thorax and induces a systemic immune response that can favor secondary infections such as pneumonia. In particular, thoracic trauma substantially increases the risk of post-traumatic pneumonia, as direct lung injury, impaired respiratory function, and the frequent need for mechanical ventilation predispose patients to pulmonary infections, thereby contributing to adverse clinical outcomes. To improve translational understanding of these interactions, complex in vitro models have been developed to experimentally dissect the biological mechanisms underlying injuries of the lung. This review provides a comprehensive overview of current in vitro lung models and their suitability to analyze trauma induced lung damage and following infection. Key methodological variables are the selection of appropriate cell lines, the modeling of air - liquid interface or barrier function and the simulation of the trauma. Importantly, experimental approaches should clearly distinguish between inflammatory stimulation and mechanical injury, as these represent distinct pathophysiological processes. Collectively, the models discussed herein highlight the importance of standardized and physiologically relevant in vitro trauma models for advancing mechanistic insights and facilitating the development of targeted therapeutic strategies.

articles.title: Physiologic, Metabolic, and Protein Redox Effects of Methylene Blue in a Porcine Hemorrhage Model.
articles.abstract: Methylene blue (MB) has established benefit in vasodilatory shock, and a potential role in hemorrhagic shock. Some evidence suggests that MB could lower anesthetic requirements. The aim of this study was to investigate the effect of MB on volatile anesthetic requirements (primary), metabolic markers (secondary), and protein redox modifications (tertiary) in a porcine hemorrhage model. This was a randomized 2 x 2 factorial animal study conducted at a tertiary medical center in 2019-2020. Forty swine were randomized to the following experimental interventions: hemorrhage (0 v. 30 mL/kg, at t = 0 min) and MB (0 v. 2 mg/kg, at t = 20 min). End-tidal isoflurane, blood pressure, and arterial blood gas parameters were recorded at prespecified intervals. Skeletal muscle was used for redox analyses. Group differences were investigated with mixed effects and one-way analyses of variance. There was no effect of MB on volatile requirements or metabolic markers (all P > 0.05). Hemorrhage was associated with 2.4 mg/dL higher lactate (95% CI, 1.4 to 3.4) and 23 mmHg lower mean arterial pressure (95% CI, 11 to 34). Hemorrhage was also associated with increased protein carbonyl levels (P < 0.001) that were non-significantly attenuated by MB (P = 0.130), and increased protein S-nitrosylation (P < 0.001) that was significantly attenuated by MB (P < 0.001). MB does not have a significant effect on volatile anesthetic requirements or systemic physiologic and metabolic responses during hemorrhagic shock. However, MB significantly attenuates protein S-nitrosylation and partially attenuates protein carbonyl accumulation.

Ultrasound-guided infraspinatus-teres minor plane block for acute post traumatic shoulder pain in the emergency department: A case series.
articles.journal: The American journal of emergency medicine
articles.abstract: Acute traumatic shoulder injuries are often associated with severe pain that hinders examination, radiographic positioning, and timely orthopaedic management. Conventional systemic analgesia may be inadequate, while interscalene and superior trunk blocks can be limited by hemidiaphragmatic paresis. The ultrasound-guided infraspinatus teres minor (ITM) inter-fascial plane block is a recently described diaphragm-sparing technique that targets the suprascapular and axillary nerves through a single posterior injection and has shown promising anatomic and postoperative analgesic coverage in earlier reports. In this case series, four patients presenting to the emergency department with acute traumatic shoulder pain refractory to multimodal systemic analgesia, received ultrasound-guided ITM block using 20-25 mL of 0.375% ropivacaine with dexamethasone; three of them also received a continuous catheter infusion of 0.2% ropivacaine. Injuries included displaced proximal humeral fracture, glenoid fracture, humeral neck fracture, and humeral head dislocation. In all cases, pain scores fell rapidly from 8 to 10/10 to 0-1/10 within 30 min, facilitating examination, imaging, plaster application, immobilization, or closed reduction without rescue analgesia or procedural sedation. Analgesia remained satisfactory during observation, and no block-related complications were reported. These preliminary findings suggest that the ITM block may be an effective and practical diaphragm-sparing option for emergency department analgesia in acute shoulder injuries, with the added advantage of catheter-based prolongation when needed. Larger prospective comparative studies are required to confirm its efficacy, define safety, and clarify its role relative to other regional techniques.

articles.title: When metabolic emergencies collide: A case of concurrent diabetic ketoacidosis and tumor lysis syndrome.
articles.journal: The American journal of emergency medicine
articles.abstract: Tumor lysis syndrome (TLS) is an oncologic emergency increasingly recognized in highly chemosensitive cancers but is not often reported in solid tumors such as small cell lung cancer (SCLC) Diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA) may occur in patients receiving chemotherapy due to glucocorticoid exposure, metabolic stress, and insulin deficiency. Concurrent TLS and DKA may present with overlapping features of shock, acidosis, and acute kidney injury, creating a diagnostic challenge for emergency physicians. An 82-year-old man with extensive-stage small cell lung cancer (ES-SCLC) receiving carboplatin, etoposide, and atezolizumab presented to the ED five days post-chemotherapy with vomiting, hypotension, and tachypnea. Evaluation revealed severe anion-gap metabolic acidosis (pH 7.17, lactate 13.9 mmol/L), hyperglycemia (466 mg/dL), ketonemia, acute kidney injury, hyperuricemia (12.5 mg/dL), and hyperphosphatemia (8.2 mg/dL), meeting Cairo-Bishop criteria for clinical TLS as well as DKA. Respiratory viral PCR was positive for rhinovirus/enterovirus. The patient required ICU admission, insulin infusion, aggressive intravenous hydration and rasburicase. This case underscores the importance of considering concurrent TLS in patients with recently treated chemosensitive malignancies who present with DKA, acute kidney injury, hyperuricemia, or hyperphosphatemia. Recognition of TLS may prompt disease-specific interventions including rasburicase administration, oncology consultation, and intensive monitoring beyond standard DKA management.

articles.title: Cardiopulmonary bone cement embolism after Percutaneous Kyphoplasty: a case series.
articles.journal: The American journal of emergency medicine
articles.abstract: Cement-induced intracardiopulmonary embolism is an uncommon but potentially serious complication after percutaneous kyphoplasty (PKP). Early recognition and timely intervention are therefore critical. We report a series of five patients with intracardiopulmonary cement embolism after PKP. For emergency physicians, cement embolism should remain an important diagnostic consideration in patients with recent PKP, particularly elderly women who present with chest discomfort or otherwise unexplained hypotension. Failure to elicit a recent history of PKP may therefore delay diagnosis. Symptomatic cement embolism may deteriorate rapidly and requires prompt hemodynamic stabilization, respiratory support, and early imaging. CT or bedside ultrasonography is essential for identifying pulmonary cement embolism and cardiac perforation. Early multidisciplinary consultation should be initiated to determine whether the patients need surgical or endovascular embolectomy.

articles.title: Telemedicine-supported pediatric burn mass casualty response in a rural emergency department.
articles.journal: The American journal of emergency medicine
articles.abstract: Mass casualty incidents (MCIs) involving pediatric burn patients are rare, high-impact events that can rapidly overwhelm rural emergency departments (EDs), particularly critical access hospitals with limited pediatric and subspecialty resources. We report a pediatric burn MCI involving three critically injured children presenting within minutes of each other to a rural ED following an enclosed structural fire. Pre-arrival EMS notification enabled early activation of institutional MCI protocols and immediate telemedicine consultation with regional pediatric and burn specialists. This facilitated rapid mobilization of multidisciplinary personnel, anticipatory airway planning, and coordination of critical care transport. Upon arrival, patients required simultaneous resuscitation under conditions of limited staffing and constrained transport availability. All three patients were stabilized and transferred to a regional pediatric burn center. Two patients survived to hospital discharge while the third was compassionately extubated at the receiving facility days later. To our knowledge, this is among the first descriptions of telemedicine-supported simultaneous pediatric burn MCI resuscitations in a critical access ED. This case highlights the importance of early MCI activation, and telemedicine-enabled operational and clinical coordination in rural disaster response systems.

articles.title: Beyond the lungs: A case series of extrapulmonary tuberculosis.
articles.journal: The American journal of emergency medicine
articles.abstract: Globally, Tuberculosis (TB) is the leading infectious cause of death with more than 10 million cases and 1 million deaths from the disease annually. TB can present as a primary extrapulmonary infection without pulmonary symptoms or infection often mimicking other pathologies, thereby making its clinical manifestations uniquely difficult to diagnose in the Emergency Department. We present five patients with rare cases of TB in an effort to underscore the importance of the EM physician keeping extrapulmonary infection in their differential. Extrapulmonary TB is a high acuity, low incidence disease that must be on EM physicians' differential when considering susceptible patient populations with common ED chief complaints. Complications from undetected disease can result in significant patient morbidity and mortality. Extrapulmonary TB is likely an underdiagnosed condition due to its often subtle and confounding presentations. The diagnosis should be considered in individuals with TB risk factors, HIV or other immunocompromised conditions, a history of TB infection and recurrent organ-specific infectious symptoms.

articles.title: Unexplained hyperammonemia in the emergency department: Late-onset ornithine transcarbamylase deficiency in a 75-year-old man.
articles.journal: The American journal of emergency medicine
articles.abstract: Late-onset ornithine transcarbamylase deficiency (OTCD) is an extremely rare X-linked urea cycle disorder in the geriatric population, and its diagnosis in the emergency department (ED) is highly challenging. We report the case of a 75-year-old man who presented to the ED with acute confusion and vomiting that rapidly progressed to coma. Initial investigations revealed unexplained hyperammonemia. Despite an empiric lactulose enema, his neurological status continued to deteriorate, and his plasma ammonia level peaked at 487 μmol/L. He required endotracheal intubation, and emergent hemodialysis was initiated. A detailed family history revealed that two nephews had died from unexplained hyperammonemia, raising a high index of suspicion for an inherited metabolic disorder. Subsequent plasma amino acid analysis revealed elevated ornithine and decreased citrulline levels. The diagnosis was confirmed by next-generation sequencing, which identified a hemizygous OTC variant (c.119G > A, p.Arg40His). The patient was successfully managed with hemodialysis, intravenous L-arginine, and a protein-restricted diet, and he was ultimately discharged without focal neurological sequelae. This case highlights that clinicians should consider urea cycle disorders in the differential diagnosis of unexplained hyperammonemia regardless of age, including in geriatric patients. Furthermore, it underscores the critical value of a comprehensive family history and the prompt initiation of hemodialysis-before genetic confirmation-to prevent irreversible neurological damage in atypical adult presentations.

articles.title: Coronary subclavian steal syndrome in the emergency department - A case report.
articles.journal: The American journal of emergency medicine
articles.abstract: Coronary Subclavian Steal Syndrome (CSSS) is a rare condition of blood flow reversal, in patients who have undergone Coronary Arterial Bypass Graft (CABG) with a Left Internal Mammary Artery (LIMA) to Left anterior descending (LAD) graft, who have concomitant left subclavian artery stenosis. The left subclavian artery stenosis results in retrograde blood flow from the coronary circulation through the LIMA- LAD graft to the left subclavian artery, causing cardiac ischemia. We report a case of a 77-year-old Female with previous CABG (LIMA to LAD graft) who presented to the Emergency department (ED) with chest pain. Her Electrocardiogram (ECG) showed ST elevations in aVR and widespread ST depressions in the anterior, lateral and inferior leads with a raised high sensitivity Troponin. A diagnosis of Non-ST Elevation Myocardial Infarction (NSTEMI) was made, and she underwent Coronary Angiogram which revealed relatively patent grafts that could not explain her presentation. She was found to have left subclavian artery stenosis and subclavian artery angioplasty was performed successfully. Coronary Subclavian Steal Syndrome is a rare but significant pathology. It is important for Emergency physicians to consider it as a differential in patients with history of CABG and suggestive clinical features. A Computed Tomography (CT) Angiogram or Aortogram should be performed, and Vascular Surgery should be activated early for timely intervention.

articles.title: Methanol toxicity from inhalational abuse of a methyl acetate-containing nail polish remover.
articles.journal: The American journal of emergency medicine
articles.abstract: Methyl acetate is an organic solvent used in certain nail polish removers that hydrolyzes in aqueous environments to liberate methanol and acetic acid. This is a case report of a 47-year-old woman who presented to the emergency department intoxicated after an episode of loss of consciousness following recreational huffing of a nail polish remover containing methyl acetate. Laboratory studies demonstrated an elevated anion-gap metabolic acidosis suggestive of methanol toxicity. Diagnosis was confirmed through measurement of the serum methanol concentration, which was 35 mg/dL (reference range < 10 mg/dL). Toxicity was managed in the emergency department with administration of fomepizole (4-methylpyrazole) and initiation of hemodialysis. After a single session of hemodialysis, the patient's acid-base status normalized, visual changes resolved, and mental status returned to baseline. The patient was subsequently discharged on hospital day 2. This is an uncommon case of acute systemic methanol poisoning from inhalation of methyl acetate resulting in profound acidemia requiring hemodialysis. This case underscores the importance of careful product review and ingredient identification in the emergency department.

articles.title: Vascular Eagle syndrome presenting with expanding cervical hematoma and acute ischemic stroke causing impending airway compromise.
articles.journal: The American journal of emergency medicine
articles.abstract: Eagle syndrome is a rare condition resulting from elongation of the styloid process or ossification of the stylohyoid ligament. While the classical variant typically presents with cervicofacial pain and dysphagia, the vascular variant may lead to compression or injury of adjacent vascular structures, resulting in transient ischemic attack, arterial dissection, or ischemic stroke. Hemorrhagic vascular complications associated with Eagle syndrome are extremely uncommon. A 26-year-old female presented to the emergency department with rapidly progressive swelling on the right side of the neck associated with respiratory distress. Initial assessment revealed stridor and persistent hypoxia with oxygen saturation of 80% despite oxygen supplementation. Physical examination demonstrated a tense, expanding cervical swelling with tracheal deviation, raising concern for impending airway compromise. Intubation was attempted under sedation; however, the patient developed hypoxic bradycardia during the procedure. Oxygenation was restored using a supraglottic airway device while preparation for emergency front-of-neck access was undertaken. CT angiography revealed a fractured elongated styloid process measuring approximately 60 mm, aneurysmal dilatation of the occipital branch of the external carotid artery, and a large cervical hematoma compressing adjacent vascular structures. CT brain demonstrated right subcortical infarction involving the corona radiata and internal capsule. The patient subsequently underwent emergency tracheostomy, evacuation of cervical hematoma, and ligation of the bleeding vessel. She was later discharged with minimal residual neurological deficits. This case highlights a rare presentation of vascular Eagle syndrome producing simultaneous hemorrhagic airway compromise and ischemic stroke. Early recognition of airway compromise and prompt multidisciplinary intervention were essential for successful management.

articles.title: A case of hidradenitis suppurativa complicated by necrotizing soft tissue infection.
articles.journal: The American journal of emergency medicine
articles.abstract: Diagnosing necrotizing soft tissue infection (NSTI) in the emergency department remains challenging and is primarily a clinical diagnosis despite the availability of decision tools and advanced imaging. In patients with Hidradenitis Suppurativa (HS), baseline skin changes, prior surgical interventions and disrupted tissue planes may obscure early findings, while presentations can mimic less severe conditions such as cellulitis, abscess, or an HS flare. We present the case of a 28-year-old man with HS on adalimumab who presented with left axillary pain and swelling at a prior HS site. He was tachycardic but afebrile with localized erythema on initial examination. On repeat evaluation 50  minutes later, the erythema had rapidly extended along the lateral thoracoabdominal wall, raising concern for NSTI. The patient underwent emergent operative exploration, which revealed copious purulent fluid with disruption of fascial plans and nonviable tissue, consistent with NSTI. His postoperative course was prolonged, requiring surgical intensive care, and he was discharged to subacute rehabilitation on hospital day 25. NSTI in patients with HS may present with subtle or nonspecific findings, and underlying disease-related changes may obscure early diagnosis. These cases require a high index of suspicion, frequent reassessment, and early surgical intervention to optimize outcomes.

articles.title: Oncoptysis as the primary presentation of metastatic melanoma: A case report.
articles.journal: The American journal of emergency medicine
articles.abstract: Malignant melanoma is an aggressive skin cancer with a strong tendency to metastasize to distant organs, including the lungs. Pulmonary metastases typically present with nonspecific respiratory symptoms such as cough and dyspnea. Oncoptysis, the expectoration of tumor tissue, has been reported in only two documented cases of melanoma, with less than 50 cases reported in the literature across all malignancies. We present the case of an 88-year-old female complaining of cough and hemoptysis upon arrival to the emergency department. Upon arrival, the patient expectorated abnormal appearing tissue, which was thought initially to be lung tissue. Chest computed tomography (CT) revealed a 8 × 7 cm mass in the right lower lobe. Pathological analysis of the mass confirmed metastatic malignant melanoma in the lungs. Given that she presented with hemoptysis and respiratory distress, antiplatelet therapy was halted to minimize bleeding while bronchodilators were initiated along with supplemental oxygen. While the hemoptysis and patient's respiratory status improved, the patient declined aggressive chemotherapy and requested hospice care at home after discussions regarding her diagnosis. This case highlights a highly unusual presentation of metastatic melanoma and adds to the sparse literature on oncoptysis. The spontaneous expectoration of tumor tissue underscores the potential for central airway involvement in pulmonary metastases. Clinically, this reinforces the importance of considering malignancy in the differential diagnosis of hemoptysis, particularly in patients with a remote history of melanoma and atypical appearing expectorated sputum. Furthermore, it contributes to our understanding of how aggressive malignant progression can manifest in rare but dramatic ways, informing both careful diagnostic evaluation and palliative management strategies.

articles.title: Concomitant assessment of immunosuppression and Herpesvirus reactivation in blood at Day 7 after ICU admission in a mixed population.
Differentiated effect of hypothermia versus normothermia after cardiac arrest by neurological status and clinical correlates of ischemic burden.
articles.abstract: The optimal temperature target after out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA) remains uncertain, as major randomized trials have not demonstrated a clear benefit of lower-target hypothermia compared with normothermia. Despite this, patients with differing degrees of ischemic burden or early neurological injury may hypothetically respond differently to temperature targets, raising the possibility of heterogeneous treatment effects. This study aimed to determine whether outcomes differ after OHCA with 33 °C versus controlled normothermia (36.0-37.7 °C) according to correlates of ischemic burden and neurological findings at hospital admission. This secondary analysis of the TTM and TTM2 trials employed effect-based machine learning to probe for heterogeneous treatment effects. Causal forests and Bayesian additive regression trees (BART) estimated individualized treatment effects (ITE) based on ischemia duration, prehospital factors, and neurological examination findings at hospital admission. Treatment effect modifier variable importance parameter (TEM-VIP) analysis ranked the baseline variables most likely to modify effect. The primary outcome was six-month all-cause mortality, and the secondary outcome was poor functional outcome (modified Rankin scale score 4-6). Primary analyses evaluated potential heterogeneity within each trial, while secondary analyses pooled all participants. All 2789 adult OHCA patients from the trials' primary analyses were included (median age 65 years (IQR 56-73), 79.9% male). Death occurred in 49.4% of patients in the 33 °C group, and in 47.9% in the controlled normothermia group. Variation in six-month mortality ITEs estimated from ischemic burden correlates and initial neurological findings was minimal, and no significant heterogeneity of treatment effect was identified across all methods and analysis populations. In the pooled analysis, estimated conditional mean mortality risk difference ranged from - 1.2% to 2.1% in causal forest (p = 0.99), and from - 0.5% to 1.5% in BART, with posterior probabilities for hypothermia benefit ranging from 42% to 53%. Absolute subgroup estimates in TEM-VIP analysis were small and non-significant. Results were consistent for the six-month functional outcome. Among TTM and TTM2 participants randomized to 33 °C versus controlled normothermia post-OHCA, no evidence of detectable heterogeneity of treatment effect based on available clinical correlates of ischemic burden or initial neurological findings was identified, with minimal estimated variation in treatment effect.

Current models of emergency general surgery care delivery in Manitoba, Canada: a cross-sectional survey.
articles.journal: World journal of emergency surgery : WJES
articles.abstract: Emergency general surgery conditions result in disproportionately high rates of morbidity and mortality. Despite this, little is known about the resources available for related care in Canadian hospitals. Our aim was to describe the resources and structures dedicated to emergency general surgery in Manitoba, Canada. We developed a survey to examine institutional capabilities in providing emergency general surgical care. The survey was developed over three iterations using a modified Delphi technique and was then reviewed separately by community surgeons to ensure broad applicability. A cross-sectional survey of representatives at each of the fourteen hospitals reported to offer emergency general surgery care in Manitoba was performed in two iterations between March and December 2023. Findings were examined descriptively and stratified between tertiary, urban, and rural centres. Our aim was to describe the resources and structures in place for providing related care, including the proportion of hospitals with a dedicated emergency general surgery care model. After exclusions and non-responses, we examined the resources and capabilities of nine institutions. Two tertiary, two urban community, and five rural community centres were evaluated. Of these institutions, 4/9 (44.4%) had an emergency general surgery model of care, including one rural centre. There was a large degree of variation in operative resources, specialty services, and physician learners between centre types. Allied health professionals were more consistently available across hospitals. Our survey results identified several pertinent gaps in care, including a lack of shared treatment protocols, transfer agreements, and quality improvement measures, even at large tertiary centres. This study demonstrates a pressing need for collaboration between centres and involvement in quality improvement amongst practitioners to meet standards of care in emergency general surgery. The results also show that important aspects of emergency general surgical care can be quantified with our survey and will serve as the basis for expanding this to a country-wide study.

articles.title: Long-Term Survival Following Extracorporeal Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation: A Two-Center Five-Year Analysis.
articles.abstract: Randomized trials have shown short-term benefit of extracorporeal cardiopulmonary resuscitation (ECPR) for refractory out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA), but the long-term durability of survival and neurological recovery after hospital discharge remains poorly defined. We performed a retrospective cohort study of consecutive patients discharged alive after ECPR for refractory VT/VF OHCA from two academic centers (University of Minnesota, USA, and Charles University, Prague) from January 2013 through December 2022. The primary outcome was 5-year survival. Secondary outcomes included neurological status by Cerebral Performance Category (CPC) and associations of age and discharge disposition with long-term outcomes. Among 728 patients treated with ECPR, 211 (29.0%) survived to discharge; 138 from Minnesota and 73 from Prague. Median follow-up was 3.9 years; 68 patients (32%) completed 5 years. No patients were lost to follow-up. Among hospital survivors, 76.9% and 67.2% were alive at 1 and 5 years, respectively, with most deaths occurring within 90 days of discharge. CPC 1-2 was present in 78.7% at discharge and remained high among survivors beyond 1 year (93.4%-94.2%). Five-year survival declined by age from 91.6% for those between 18-39 years to 52.9% for >70 years. Discharge disposition also strongly stratified long-term prognosis. Among patients discharged alive after ECPR for refractory OHCA, long-term survival was substantial, with approximately two-thirds alive at 5 years with favorable CPC in most. Younger age and discharge home or to acute rehabilitation identified subgroups with particularly favorable prognosis. These findings support the long-term durability of benefit among selected patients treated within established ECPR systems of care.

articles.title: Post-resuscitation ST-segment elevation and coronary angiographic phenotypes in angiography-evaluable survivors of out-of-hospital cardiac arrest with presumed coronary lesion-related arrest.
articles.abstract: The clinical meaning of post-resuscitation ST-segment elevation in out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA) patients with suspected coronary etiology remains uncertain. We aimed to describe coronary angiographic phenotypes and clinical outcomes according to post-resuscitation ST-segment findings in an angiography-evaluable subset of OHCA survivors with presumed coronary lesion-related arrest. We retrospectively analyzed 149 successfully resuscitated OHCA patients admitted to our institution between January 2015 and December 2023, who underwent post-resuscitation coronary angiography and had presumed culprit lesions, defined by integrating angiographic findings with electrocardiographic, echocardiographic, and biomarker data in the clinical context. Patients were classified according to the presence or absence of post-resuscitation ST-segment elevation. ST-segment elevation was associated with a more acute occlusive coronary phenotype, with more impaired culprit-vessel flow and greater myocardial injury. In contrast, patients without ST-segment elevation more frequently had multivessel disease and chronic total occlusion, suggesting more complex coronary artery disease. Favorable neurological outcome was less frequent with ST-segment elevation in unadjusted analyses, but this association was not independent of pre-hospital factors. In this selected OHCA subset, post-resuscitation ST-segment elevation was associated with an acute occlusive coronary phenotype and greater myocardial injury, as in non-arrest acute coronary syndromes. However, the absence of ST-segment elevation did not exclude a coronary culprit lesion, so comprehensive coronary assessment is essential. ST-segment elevation was not independently associated with clinical outcomes after adjustment for pre-hospital factors. These findings should be interpreted considering substantial selection inherent to the study population.

articles.title: Timing matters: Delayed surgery increases mortality for blunt hollow viscus injury.
articles.journal: The journal of trauma and acute care surgery
articles.abstract: Immediate surgical exploration is recommended for suspected hollow viscus injury (HVI) following blunt trauma. However, diagnostic uncertainty can lead to delayed operative management. We aimed to evaluate if delayed bowel resection/repair (DBR), defined as ≥8 hours after emergency department arrival, was independently associated with increased mortality in blunt trauma patients. We also sought to identify risk factors associated with DBR. The Trauma Quality Improvement Program database (2017-2024) was queried for admitted adults with blunt abdominal trauma (abdomen abbreviated injury scale grade ≥2) who underwent bowel resection/repair. Patients who were transferred from another facility or died within 8 hours were excluded. Patients undergoing early bowel resection <8 hours (EBR) were compared with patients undergoing DBR (≥8 h). Multivariable logistic regression evaluated the association between DBR and mortality, controlling for age, severe head and thoracic injury, intubation within 1 hour of arrival, injury to the small bowel, colon, or rectum, and blood transfusion within 4 hours. Of 33,728 patients undergoing bowel resection/repair, 16,010 (47.5%) underwent DBR. The DBR cohort had lower rates of small bowel (49.6% vs. 53.9%, p<0.001) and colon (46.7% vs. 49.7%, p<0.001) injuries, but similar rates of rectal injury (4.4% vs. 4.1%, p=0.166). Injuries to the liver (26.8% vs. 20.8%), spleen (28.2% vs. 23.4%), and kidney (12.9% vs. 9.0%) were more frequent in the DBR cohort (all p<0.001). DBR patients had an increased associated risk of mortality (13.0% vs. 8.5%, OR 1.21, 95% CI: 1.12-1.30, p<0.001). Small bowel injury was the only independent factor with decreased associated risk of DBR (OR 0.93, CI: 0.89-0.97, p=0.001). Delayed operative management for blunt HVI occurs more often in patients with solid organ injuries and is independently associated with increased mortality. These findings highlight the importance of early detection and timely surgical management of HVI. Therapeutic/Care Management, Level IV.

articles.title: Individualized treatment effects of high flow nasal oxygen in immunocompromised patients.
articles.abstract: High flow nasal oxygen (HFNO) has become a common first-line practice for acute hypoxemic respiratory failure (ARF). In immunocompromised patients, ARF is the leading cause of ICU admission, yet a randomized trial found no overall benefit of HFNO in this population. To assess whether baseline characteristics influence HFNO's effectiveness in preventing invasive mechanical ventilation (IMV) in immunocompromised patients with ARF. A causal forest machine-learning algorithm was derived in the HIGH trial (776 patients randomized to HFNO or conventional oxygen) to predict the HFNO effects on day-28 IMV incidence. Patients with a "do-not-intubate" order (n = 72) were excluded. Model performance was validated through 500 bootstrap iterations and patients were categorized into terciles based on predicted HFNO benefit. Transportability of the model was assessed in an independent observational cohort (818 patients). Among the 704 participants, HFNO's average effect on day-28 IMV was not significant. However, substantial heterogeneity in treatment responses was identified (predicted benefit: from 20.2% [IQR 15.5%-23.9%] absolute IMV risk reduction with HFNO to 7.4% risk reduction [2.9%-11.2%] with conventional oxygen). Patients with the highest predicted benefit were older, more frequently solid organ transplant recipients, less neutropenic, more severely hypoxemic/tachycardic, but with lower non-respiratory sequential organ failure assessment (SOFA) scores. In this subgroup, HFNO was associated with a significant lower incidence of IMV. In the observational cohort, the benefit-ranking performance was preserved, although absolute effect estimates were less calibrated. These results suggest HFNO might benefit specific immunocompromised patients with ARF. Further prospective studies are needed to validate these findings.
