Initial visual acuity, lens status, optic disc involvement, secondary glaucoma, eye surgery performed, OTS score and posterior segment injury were statistically significant in predicting final visual outcomes. Additionally, this study emphasizes how important it is to use protective glasses when playing badminton.

articles.title: Outcomes of circular frame external fixation for tibia fracture in the elderly: comparison with a fracture-matched younger cohort.
articles.abstract: Circular frame fixation is a management method often used for complex fractures, or fractures with soft tissue compromise. Tibia fractures in older adults can be difficult to manage due to an association with osteoporosis, poor quality soft tissues, and a requirement for post-operative weight bearing to maintain function and independence. There is a paucity of evidence for the use of circular frames for tibia fractures in older adults. The available evidence suggests it is an effective treatment option, however, no study has compared treatment outcomes between older and younger patients. To compare adverse events and outcomes between an 'older' cohort and 'younger' cohort of patients managed with circular frame for tibia fracture. The 'younger' cohort aged 18-50 and the 'older' cohort aged over 64 were identified from our institutional database. Injuries were classified using the AO/OTA and Gustilo-Anderson classifications. Data collection was retrospective and extracted from patient records. Adverse events were classified according to Paley as problems, obstacles or complications. Statistical analysis was performed, and significance set at p < 0.05. 135 patients were included; 66 in the 'younger' cohort and 69 in the 'older' cohort. There were significantly more females in the 'older' cohort, with a higher proportion having systemic co-morbidity (85% vs 24%) and diabetes (25% vs 3%). There were more smokers in the 'younger' cohort (33% vs 12%). There was no significant difference in rate of or time to union. The 'younger' cohort was more likely to require further procedures to achieve union. More patients in the 'older' cohort suffered a problem (30% vs 3%); pin site infection accounted for all problems in the 'older' group, and half the problems in the 'younger' group. The rate of obstacles and complications was not different CONCLUSION: Circular frame fixation is a suitable management option for 'older' patients who sustain tibia fracture, as there is no difference between rate or time to union when compared to a 'younger' cohort. 'Older' patients are more likely to encounter pin site infection and should be counselled regarding this. There is no difference between rate of more significant obstacles or complication.

articles.title: Treatment and outcome of proximal femur fractures in a resource limited setting: a prospective observational study in rural Tanzania.
articles.abstract: Proximal femur fractures are a common type of fracture worldwide and are known to result in high disability and mortality rates. In resource-limited settings, these fractures are suspected to be an underreported problem. This study provides an overview of the different treatment modalities and outcomes of patients with a proximal femur fracture in rural Tanzania. A prospective observational study was conducted in a rural referral hospital in Tanzania. Between August 2019 and August 2020 patients admitted with a proximal femur fracture were included. Data on fracture type, treatment and outcome were collected up to one year after admission. Outcome included mortality, disability (Harris Hip Score (HHS), WHODAS 2.0) and Quality of Life (EQ-5D-3L, QoL). Diagnosis: forty-seven patients were included, with a median age of 70 years (IQR 58-81). Thirty patients (30/47, 64%) sustained their injury due to a fall from standing height and eight patients were involved in a motor traffic accident. Eleven patients (11/47, 23%) sustained a femoral neck fracture, 24 patients (51%) sustained an intertrochanteric fracture and five patients (11%) sustained a subtrochanteric fracture. Five patients had additional injuries. eleven patients (11/47, 23%) received no treatment; 27 patients (57%) were treated conservatively; seven patients (15%) received an intramedullary nail. One Girdlestone (2%) was performed and one patient (2%) was referred to another hospital for operative treatment. The one-year follow-up rate was 96% (45/47). One-year mortality rate was 28% (13/47). Eleven patients (11/32, 34%) recovered to the disability level as reported prior to the injury (WHODAS 2.0). The HHS score showed a poor result in 21 patients (21/32, 66%; mean 62, SD 18). Seven patients had regained normal squat function. The QoL VAS at 3 months after admission was comparable to pre-injury reported general perceived health. Most of the patients with proximal femur fractures are treated non-operatively and not according the current standard of care which is operative fixation or arthroplasty, resulting in limited functional outcome and high mortality rates. This data shows the importance of increased attention and the need for urgent improvement of fracture treatment and outcome in resource-limited settings.

articles.title: Development of zein-coated Ag-NPs integrated into decellularized fish skin extracellular matrix as a hybrid scaffold for wound healing: In-vitro and in vivo study.
articles.abstract: Chronic wounds complicated by bacterial infections and poor tissue regeneration continue to present a major clinical problem in wound healing. This work describes a new hybrid scaffold made from zein-coated silver nanoparticles (Zein-Ag NPs) embedded in decellularized fish skin extracellular matrix (ECM). This scaffold has been designed to synergistically provide antimicrobial activity and enhance tissue repair. The Ag NPs were synthesized by chemically reducing silver nitrate with sodium borohydride and then coated with zein to improve the stability and biocompatibility of the Ag NPs. Upon evaluating the Ag NPs using dynamic light scattering (DLS), scanning electron microscopy (SEM), transmission electron microscopy (TEM), Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR), and X-ray diffraction (XRD), it was determined that optimal Ag NPs were produced using a silver nitrate precursor concentration of 5 mM, which produced nanoparticles of ~35 nm in diameter. The fish skin ECM was decellularized using the optimized physical method. The Zein-Ag/ECM scaffolds exhibited strong antimicrobial activity in vitro against Candida species and bacteria, including Staphylococcus aureus, Escherichia coli, and Pseudomonas aeruginosa, when tested using disk diffusion assays, and their controlled release of Ag⁺ minimized cytotoxicity. The biocompatibility of the material (hemocompatibility) was determined to be < 5% in vitro at 5 mM. Additionally, the material demonstrated support for the growth of fibroblasts in vitro. In vivo studies in rats showed that using the material to treat excisional wounds led to accelerated healing of the wounds, i.e., 90-95% healed by day 14, increased re-epithelialization, decreased inflammation, and improved organization of the collagen deposition in the wound site. Histopathology (using H&E and Masson Trichrome staining) confirmed this.

articles.title: Socioeconomic impact of upper and lower extremity fractures among temporary migrant workers: A prospective longitudinal cohort study.
articles.abstract: Temporary migrant workers may be particularly vulnerable to financial and occupational consequences after fracture. This study evaluated longitudinal income changes and socioeconomic outcomes following appendicular fractures in this population. This prospective cohort study included temporary migrant workers in Kuwait aged 18-65 years presenting with appendicular fractures between January 2023 and January 2025. Pre-injury income and income at 1, 3, 6 and 12 months were recorded and expressed as a percentage of individual baseline income. Unadjusted and exploratory multivariable analyses examined complete income loss at 12 months. Of 601 patients assessed, 430 were included. Complete income loss affected 19.1% at 1 month, peaked at 35.1% at 3 months and persisted in 23.3% at 12 months. Mean income retained at 12 months was 65.8% of baseline: 55.5% in physically demanding labour versus 80.1% in professional roles. By 12 months, 77.0% had returned to work, but 58.0% of returners earned less than before injury. Self-employment (adjusted OR 3.02; 95% CI 1.57-5.82) and multiple fractures (2.21; 1.25-3.92) remained associated with complete income loss after adjustment; the occupational association was attenuated. Appendicular fractures were followed by persistent socioeconomic disruption, with greater observed income deficits among physically demanding and self-employed workers and those with more extensive injuries. Returners often remained below baseline income at 12 months. Recovery assessment should include income and occupational stability.

articles.title: Effect of AI-assisted radiographic fracture detection on paediatric emergency department length of stay through fracture exclusion: A before-after cohort study.
articles.abstract: Artificial intelligence-assisted radiographic fracture detection tools (AI-RFDT) have the potential to support confident fracture exclusion by physicians in the paediatric emergency department (ED), where presentations for suspected fractures substantially outnumber confirmed fractures. This study aimed to evaluate whether implementation of AI-RFDT in a paediatric ED is associated with reduced length of stay (LOS) among patients presenting with suspected fractures, and to determine whether any observed effect is specifically mediated through the fracture-exclusion pathway. This retrospective before-after cohort study was conducted at a single tertiary paediatric ED. AI-RFDT (BoneView, Gleamer, Paris, France) was deployed on 1 October 2023 as a passive, second-read decision-support tool. The study population comprised 4172 paediatric patients with rule-out fracture diagnoses (fracture-excluded; F-E) during standard working hours (08:00-15:59; pre-AI n = 2514; post-AI n = 1658). Fracture-confirmed (F-C) patients served as a pre-specified internal control (n = 1155). The primary outcome was ED LOS; secondary outcomes were orthopaedic consultation rate, LOS by consultation status, anatomical subgroup LOS, and 30-day re-admission. Orthopaedic consultation rates in the paediatric ED decreased from 73% to 68.3% (Δ -4.7 %age points, p = 0.002). The greatest reduction was observed in patients discharged without orthopaedic consultation (2.25→1.78 h, Δ -28 min, p < 0.001), while those with confirmed fractures demonstrated no significant change in LOS (Δ+3 min, p = 0.51). 30-day re-admission rates remained unchanged (6.9% vs 6.9%, p = 1.00). Wrist and forearm injuries demonstrated the greatest LOS reduction (Δ -24 min, p = 0.004). Deployment of AI-RFDT in a paediatric ED was associated with a reduction in LOS that was concentrated among patients discharged without orthopaedic consultation. The absence of LOS change in confirmed-fracture controls supports a mechanism specific to fracture exclusion rather than generalised care acceleration.

articles.title: Birthday Blues: Clinical Patterns of Emergency Department Visits Surrounding Birthdays.
articles.abstract: Smaller studies have suggested that patients are more likely to present to the emergency department around the time of their birthdays. However, no multi-year analysis has been performed within the U.S. to uncover a possible association between birthdays and presentation to the emergency department (ED). The objective of this study was to evaluate the overall frequency year after year of visits to the Emergency Department and the medical conditions most frequently encountered around the time of a birthday. We studied emergency department visits from May 2018 to May 2024 at a Level 1 Trauma Center in a metropolitan city in the U.S.. Our analysis assessed the interval before or after ED presentation with respect to a patient's birthday. We utilized timeframes of ± 7 days (7 d) of one's birthday, ± 14 days (14 d), and ± 30 days (30 d) for analysis. We then conducted a descriptive analysis comparing proportions, standardized ratios (SR), and obtaining predictive probabilities from a multivariate logistic regression model. Of the 310,047 unique ED visits from 2018 to 2024, 12,650 visits were within ±7d of a patient's birthday. There were a greater than expected number of presentations ±7 d for all genders and age groups (particularly those <18 years old), and for those identifying as Asians. When looking at the role of chief complaint, individuals with a chief complaint related to Psychiatric/Toxicology, Trauma, Dermatologic, and Musculoskeletal concerns had a higher incidence of ED presentation ±7 d. Across all populations, birthdays appear to be associated with an elevated risk of serious illness.

articles.title: Incidence of severe mountain bike-related injuries and mortality: A 15-year statewide analysis.
articles.abstract: Mountain biking has grown in popularity and has seen widespread trail development but carries risk for severe trauma. No studies have analysed severe injuries in the context of contemporary mountain biking to understand trends and modifiable risk factors. To describe the incidence and longitudinal characteristics of severe injuries related to mountain biking in Tasmania, Australia. Retrospective analysis of all patients admitted to Tasmanian public hospitals with severe mountain bike (MTB)-related injuries from 1st January 2010-31 st December 2024. Incidence of severe MTB-related injuries (including mortality) as defined by hospital admission to an intensive care unit or neurosurgery high dependency unit; for emergency surgery (in <4 h); or transfer intra- or interstate for definitive treatment. Secondary outcomes were annual injury trends in mechanism of injury, body regions, injury profiles, and incident location. For the total period there were 85 severe injuries (including 4 mortalities) from 6643 MTB-related emergency department (ED) presentations. Annual severe MTB-related cases increased over the 15 years from 0.8 cases/year before 2015, to 8.1 cases/year in later years. Severe injury cases accounted for only 1.3% of all MTB-related ED presentations. Most severely injured riders were male (97%); the mean age was 36 years (SD 16.9) for the total period, but this increased from 18.5 years (SD 5.8) pre-2015-36.9 years (SD 16.8) post-2015. Executing a jump was the dominant mechanism of injury (44%), followed by fall over handlebars (14%), obstacle collision (11%) and adverse trail conditions (9%). The most injured body regions were abdomen (31%), neck (23%) and thorax/chest (20%). The most common types of injuries were fracture/dislocation (44%), abdominal organ injury (24%) and thoracic organ injury (15%). Spinal cord injury occurred in 6% of cases and traumatic brain injury in 7%. Over 50% of severe injury incidents occurred on purpose-built MTB trails. Severe MTB-related injuries increased proportionally to all MTB-related injuries suggesting the increase was largely driven by rider exposure. Targeted injury prevention strategies, safe trail design, and understanding risk factors are needed to ensure safe progression of this popular sport.

articles.title: Surgeon preferences and educational gaps in the treatment of complex distal radius fractures in Latin America.
articles.abstract: Distal radius fractures are among the most common skeletal injuries, yet their optimal treatment remains controversial. Variability in surgical decision-making has been observed among surgeons. This study aimed to identify treatment preferences among Latin American orthopaedic surgeons with different training backgrounds and levels of experience in the management of complex distal radius fractures. A two-part questionnaire was distributed to orthopaedic and hand surgeons across Latin America. The first section collected demographic data, and the second section presented 7 clinical scenarios involving complex distal radius fractures. Multivariate analysis using multinomial logistic regression was performed to assess the influence of age and fellowship training on treatment decision-making, with results expressed as odds ratios. P-values < 0.05 were considered statistically significant. A total of 617 completed questionnaires were analyzed. Most respondents were male orthopaedic surgeons with fellowship training in orthopaedic trauma or hand surgery. Most surgeons reported managing 10-25 distal radius fracture cases annually as the lead surgeon and had access to both anatomical angle-stable volar plates and fragment-specific implants. Older surgeons tended to favor more traditional techniques, whereas those with hand surgery fellowship training were more likely to adopt advanced fixation strategies and a broader range of surgical approaches. Surgeon age and fellowship training in hand surgery were the most influential factors in treatment decision-making for complex distal radius fractures. These findings highlight an opportunity for AO Trauma Latin America to expand educational offerings focused on the treatment of complex distal radius fractures.

articles.title: Corrigendum to "Modified Masquelet technique using free vascularized fibula grafting for reconstruction of large bone defects after bone infection" [Injury 57(3) (2026) 113036].
Can radiological parameters predict failure of fixation in distal radius fractures treated with a volar locking plate?
articles.abstract: Fractures of the distal radius are common, and volar locking plates are the most utilized fixation method. Failure of fixation, defined as post-operative fracture collapse leading to loss of reduction and/or screw penetration, is an undesirable outcome. We aimed to demonstrate whether preoperative and intraoperative radiographic parameters are associated with subsequent failure of fixation in order to produce a model that may be able to predict failure. A retrospective case-control study of 23 cases of failure of fixation matched to controls from the same cohort by age, sex, and AO classification in a 3:1 ratio. Nine initial injury and 13 intraoperative radiological parameters were evaluated, and multi-variate regression analysis models were analysed to assess if they could reliably predict failure. A total of 92 patients were analysed (23 cases, 69 controls). Size of intraarticular gap was the only preoperative parameter to be associated failure with every 0.47 mm increase in fracture gap resulting in a 1.6 increase of odds ratio of failure. Based on intraoperative radiological parameters, three factors were associated with failure: dorsal capitate translation, intraarticular gap and step. Models based on these parameters do not accurately predict failure, however, models based on intraoperative factors are associated with risk of failure with high specificity but low sensitivity. We conclude that the severity of the injury is less importantly associated with failure of fixation, whereas the quality of the surgical fixation and specifically the accuracy of the reduction are more important.

articles.title: Association of neighborhood social vulnerability with reoperation after operative treatment of proximal humerus fractures.
articles.abstract: Neighborhood-level indices may capture different dimensions of social risk. We evaluated whether the Social Vulnerability Index (SVI) was associated with reoperation after operative treatment of acute proximal humerus fractures (PHFs), using the Area Deprivation Index (ADI) as a secondary comparator. This retrospective cohort included 438 distinct fracture episodes treated within a single United States practice group from January 2021 through December 2024. The outcome was ipsilateral shoulder reoperation for a postoperative complication. Primary logistic regression models adjusted for age, American Society of Anesthesiologists class, and diabetes mellitus; ADI analyses included 414 fractures. Fifty-one fractures (11.6%) underwent reoperation. Reoperation increased from 6.4% to 16.1% across SVI quartiles (ordered trend P = 0.028; omnibus P = 0.163). Each 0.10 increase in SVI was associated with reoperation in the primary model (odds ratio [OR], 1.13; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.01-1.26; P = 0.033) and after adjustment for procedure category (OR, 1.13; 95% CI, 1.01-1.26; P = 0.027). ADI national and state ranks were not associated with reoperation. Higher SVI was associated with reoperation, whereas ADI national and state ranks were not. These index-specific, hypothesis-generating findings require external validation.

articles.title: Signs of Life and Clinical Outcomes in Patients With Traumatic Out-of-Hospital Cardiac Arrest: A Nationwide Multicenter Observational Study.
articles.abstract: The prognostic value of individual signs of life (SOLs) remains unclear in patients experiencing traumatic out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (t-OHCA). To describe clinical outcomes among patients with t-OHCA by the presence of each SOL at the scene. Data from the SOS-KANTO 2017 study, a multicenter prospective registry of OHCA cases treated between 2019 and 2021, were retrospectively analyzed. Adult patients diagnosed with t-OHCA were included, excluding those with a palpable pulse upon emergency medical service (EMS) arrival. Patients were categorized into eight subgroups based on the presence of three SOLs at the scene-the pupillary light reflex, spontaneous respiration, and cardiac electrical activity - and descriptive analyses were performed. The primary outcome was survival beyond the emergency department (ED). Of the 462 patients included in the analysis, two (0.4%) exhibited all three SOLs, and 18 (3.9%) exhibited two SOLs; in the latter group, two demonstrated cardiac activity and a pupillary reflex, and 16 had cardiac activity and spontaneous respiration. Among the 124 patients (26.8%) with only one SOL, 117 had cardiac activity, three showed a pupillary reflex, and four exhibited spontaneous respiration. No SOLs were observed in 318 patients (68.8%). Overall, 22 patients (4.8%) survived beyond the ED. The highest survival rate was observed in the subgroup with both cardiac activity and spontaneous respiration (4/16; 25%), followed by the subgroup with cardiac activity alone (10/117; 8.5%). Among the t-OHCA patients, survival beyond the ED was observed more frequently in those with cardiac electrical activity at the scene.

articles.title: Force measurement in circular external fixation frames reflects construct stability: A laboratory proof-of-concept study.
articles.abstract: Circular external fixation frames are widely used in limb reconstruction, however determining the optimal time for frame removal remains challenging. Current approaches rely on clinical and radiological assessment, both of which have recognised limitations. Mechanical assessment of construct stability offers a potential alternative, but existing approaches have not translated widely into clinical practice, in part due to reliance on absolute measurement thresholds. To determine whether force measurement within a circular external fixation frame varies systematically with fracture site stability, and to assess whether this measurement may support monitoring of healing progression. Three similar four-ring Ilizarov frame constructs were assembled using a Perspex bone analogue. A load cell was integrated into the frame and used to measure force during axial loading to 700 N. Models representing different stages of fracture healing were simulated using varying fracture gaps and materials of differing stiffness. Measurements were obtained across multiple sensor positions and configurations. Force measurements were compared between models using non-parametric statistical methods. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis was performed to assess separation between conditions. Force measured within the frame decreased progressively with increasing construct stiffness. A significant relationship between model stability and measured force was observed (Kruskal-Wallis p < 0.0001). Clear separation was demonstrated between grossly unstable and intact constructs; however, overlap between higher stability models and intact bone was evident. ROC analysis showed strong discrimination when considering all unstable conditions (AUC ≥ 0.91), but performance was reduced when restricted to higher stability models (AUC 0.699-0.838). Absolute force measurements varied with sensor configuration, although the rank order of conditions was preserved. Force measurement within a circular external fixation frame reflects construct stability in an in vitro model. Whilst absolute values are dependent on construct configuration and show reduced discrimination near union, consistent directional changes suggest that serial within-subject measurement may provide a useful approach to monitoring healing progression. These findings support further evaluation of longitudinal measurement strategies in clinical studies.

articles.title: Screening for posttraumatic stress symptoms after accidental injury: Implementation of the young child PTSD screen in the acute trauma setting.
articles.abstract: Post-traumatic stress symptoms (PTSS) in young children are underrecognized following unintentional injury, and validated screening tools for early childhood are rarely implemented in acute trauma settings. We evaluated the Young Child PTSD Screen (YCPS) administered at hospital discharge to determine screening positivity, associated clinical factors, and persistence of symptoms at one month. We conducted a retrospective cohort study of children aged 2-6 years admitted to a Level I pediatric trauma center following unintentional injury (November 2020-November 2024). Caregivers completed the 6-item YCPS at discharge. Children with ≥ 1 endorsed symptom were contacted one month later for repeat assessment. Demographic, injury, and hospitalization data were abstracted from the trauma registry and electronic health record. Multivariable logistic regression evaluated predictors of positive screening at discharge, and follow-up analyses assessed persistence of symptoms. Of 193 screened patients, 186 met inclusion criteria. Over half (55.9%, n = 104) screened symptomatic or positive at discharge. On univariate analysis, greater injury severity score and longer length of stay were associated with symptomatic/positive screening. In multivariable analysis, injury severity remained the only significant predictor (aOR 1.07 per point increase in injury severity score, 95% CI 1.02-1.13, p = 0.004). Of eligible children, 32.6% (n = 34) completed one-month follow-up and 41.1% (n = 14) screened positive. Higher discharge YCPS scores were associated with positive follow-up (median 3 vs 2; p = 0.046) and were positively correlated with one-month scores (r²=0.21, p = 0.005). No demographic variables (age, sex, race) predicted persistence of symptoms. Over one-third of traumatically injured young children screened positive for PTSS at discharge, and a substantial proportion had persistent symptoms at one month. Injury severity was associated with positive screens at discharge, while early symptom burden predicted persistence. These findings support the feasibility and clinical value of implementing developmentally sensitive screening for very young children in the inpatient trauma setting.

articles.title: Clinical equipoise as inclusion criterion to control for confounding in observational studies.
articles.abstract: This study investigates whether higher levels of expert disagreement, as a proxy for clinical equipoise, are associated with improved baseline comparability between treatment groups in patients with proximal humerus fractures. Additionally, it aimed to assess how progressively stricter inclusion criteria-based on this disagreement-affect the distribution of baseline characteristics between the treatment groups. We used data from the LADON Humerus study, a multicentre, prospective cohort including patients treated operatively or non-operatively in five hospitals in the Netherlands and Switzerland. An international expert panel of trauma surgeons assessed anonymized cases, blinded to the actual treatment, and each expert gave a treatment recommendation. Disagreement between the treatment given and the expert recommendations was categorized into four levels (A: complete disagreement, B: partial disagreement, C: partial agreement, D: complete agreement). Standardized differences (StDiff) for age, sex, ASA score, and AO classification were used to assess comparability between treatment groups across disagreement levels. A total of 351 patients were included in the analysis. Comparability between treatment groups improved as the level of disagreement increased. At complete disagreement (Level A), the groups were well balanced with respect to age, sex, and ASA score (StDiff ≤ 0.1). For AO classification, group comparability improved but remained insufficiently balanced at the highest level of disagreement. Stricter inclusion criteria resulted in improved balance at the cost of reduced sample size. Using expert panel disagreement as inclusion criterion can enhance group comparability in observational research. This approach may reduce the potential for confounding when RCTs are not possible.

articles.title: Epidemiological patterns and surgical outcomes of pediatric supracondylar humerus fractures: a focus on domestic safety and seasonal variations.
articles.abstract: Supracondylar humerus fractures (SHFs) are prevalent pediatric elbow injuries. This study investigates the epidemiology, clinical characteristics, and treatment outcomes of pediatric SHFs to identify preventive strategies. This retrospective study included 298 pediatric patients (aged ≤14 years) treated for SHFs between December 2018 and June 2024. Demographic data, injury mechanisms, seasonal variations, and surgical details were analyzed. Radiological reduction was assessed via the Baumann angle and anterior humeral line. Functional outcomes were evaluated using Flynn's criteria. The study cohort (mean age 6.1 years; 58.7% male) predominantly sustained extension-type fractures (96.3%), with the severely displaced Gartland Type III being the most frequent (49.3%). The incidence of injuries peaked during the summer months and school holidays, with the majority occurring at home (64.1%) due to simple falls (93%). Surgical intervention, consisting of closed reduction and percutaneous pinning, was necessitated in 75.8% of cases, with a mean time-to-surgery of 4.6 h. Satisfactory (excellent and good) functional outcomes were achieved in 97.9% of the patients. Overall complication rates were minimal, and transient nerve injuries (2%) fully resolved spontaneously during follow-up. Pediatric SHFs frequently occur in domestic settings during the summer months, strongly highlighting the need for "safe home" modifications and parental education. Despite a high prevalence of severely displaced fractures, prompt surgical intervention and meticulous anatomical reduction yield excellent long-term functional outcomes and minimize complications.

articles.title: Occlusion Myocardial Infarction Missed by ST-Elevation Myocardial Infarction (STEMI) Criteria: An Angiographic Emergency Department Cohort.
articles.abstract: The ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI)/non-STEMI (NSTEMI) paradigm uses ST-elevation as a surrogate for acute coronary occlusion, but ST-elevation criteria miss many occlusions. The occlusion myocardial infarction (OMI) vs. non-occlusion (NOMI) paradigm classifies patients by the presence of an acute occlusion. To compare the 2 paradigms in an angiography-selected emergency department (ED) cohort of acute myocardial infarction. Retrospective single-center cohort of consecutive adults given an ED diagnosis of STEMI or NSTEMI who underwent coronary angiography between December 2021 and October 2023. OMI was defined as an acute culprit lesion with thrombolysis in myocardial infarction (TIMI) 0 to 2 flow, or culprit stenosis above 70% with a peak emergency department high-sensitivity troponin I above 10,000 ng/L. Of 1052 patients, 458 (43.5%) were STEMI and 594 (56.5%) NSTEMI; 837 (79.6%) met the study OMI definition. The OMI definition was met by 430 of 594 NSTEMI patients (72.4%), and 430 of 837 OMI patients (51.4%) were STEMI-negative; 51 of 458 STEMI patients (11.1%) had no occlusion. Median peak ED troponin was 155 ng/L in STEMI(+)OMI and 639 ng/L in STEMI(-)OMI (p < 0.001); median ejection fraction was 50% in both (p = 0.004). Angiography within 2 h was performed in 85.7% of STEMI(+)OMI and 15.6% of STEMI(-)OMI patients (p < 0.001). In this angiography-selected cohort, more than half of the patients who met the study OMI definition were STEMI-negative, and these patients reached angiography far later than STEMI-positive patients with occlusion. Whether such patients can be recognized before angiography requires prospective validation of prespecified electrocardiogram (ECG) criteria.

articles.title: Patient centered outcomes after surgical stabilization of rib fractures: A prospective cohort study.
articles.abstract: Rib fractures are associated with pain, impaired physical function, and reduced quality of life. Surgical stabilization of rib fractures (SSRF) is established for flail chest and ventilator-dependent patients, but its impact on longer-term patient-reported outcomes in broader injury patterns remains unclear. We evaluated whether SSRF is associated with improved physical functioning and pain outcomes compared to nonoperative management. We conducted a prospective observational cohort study of trauma ICU patients with rib fractures admitted between June 2023 and August 2024 at a single Level I trauma center. Patients met institutional criteria for SSRF, including flail chest, ≥ 3 contiguous rib fractures, or ventilator failure. Outcomes were assessed using the SF-36 and SF-MPQ-2 at discharge, 2 weeks, 3 months, and 6 months. Multivariable linear regression adjusted for RibScore, flail chest, ISS, age, obesity, hospital length of stay, and associated injuries. Primary outcomes were SF-36 physical functioning and SF-MPQ-2 present pain intensity (PPI). Of 121 patients, 39 (32%) underwent SSRF. The SSRF group had greater chest injury severity, including higher RibScores and more pneumothorax and hemothorax, while overall injury severity and demographics were similar. There were no differences in ICU length of stay, hospital length of stay, ventilator days, or mortality. After adjustment, SSRF was associated with improved physical functioning at discharge (β 13.29, 95% CI 6.53-20.05; p < 0.001) and at 6 months (β 23.40, 95% CI 7.52-39.28; p = 0.005). SSRF was associated with lower pain at discharge, but not at 6 months. SSRF was associated with improved short-term and six-month physical functioning without differences in inpatient outcomes or sustained differences in pain. These findings suggest SSRF may primarily accelerate functional recovery rather than provide durable pain reduction. II Study type: Prospective Cohort.

articles.title: A tourniquet is a good thing for continued arterial bleeding in a severely traumatized lower limb.
Evaluation of the wound healing effects of a hydrogel containing hydroalcoholic extract of Chelidonium majus in a rat model.
articles.abstract: This study aimed to develop an innovative wound dressing by loading Chelidonium majus L. extract into an alginate hydrogel matrix and to assess its efficacy in wound healing. The extract of C. majus, famous for its anti-inflammatory and antioxidant features, was obtained from plant material collected in Mazandaran Province, Iran, and incorporated into sodium alginate hydrogels at concentrations of 2% and 5% w/w. The hydrogel formulations were characterized in terms of their morphological, thermal, and swelling properties, demonstrating interconnected porous structures, altered thermal behavior indicating increased amorphous content, and high moisture absorption capacity. To evaluate biological activity, the antioxidant and flavonoid content of the extract were measured, showing notable free radical scavenging ability and high levels of flavonoids. An in vivo wound healing model using adult male Wistar rats compared the effectiveness of control, bare hydrogel, C. majus-loaded hydrogels (2% and 5%), and diltiazem treatments. Wounds treated with the 5% C. majus hydrogel showed accelerated closure rates and improved tissue regeneration, as confirmed by histological examination and enhanced expression of proliferative and regenerative genes (TGF-β) alongside decreased inflammatory markers (TNF-α and IL-1β), in comparison with the control group. These results indicate that C. majus-loaded alginate hydrogel, especially at a 5% concentration, promotes wound healing through offering a wet environment, supporting cell proliferation, and modulating inflammation. This hydrogel may represent a promising topical therapeutic option for treating skin wounds.

articles.title: Predictors of prolonged emergency department length of stay in severely injured pediatric patients.
articles.abstract: Prolonged emergency department length of stay (ED-LOS) in severely injured pediatric patients has been associated with adverse clinical outcomes. The determinants of the prolonged length of stay in severely injured pediatric patients remain incompletely understood. This study aims to identify patient-, injury-, and system-level predictors of prolonged ED-LOS among severely injured pediatric trauma patients. Data for this analysis were obtained from a multicenter trauma registry. We retrospectively analyzed prospectively collected data from the Abu Dhabi Trauma Registry over a 10-year period (2014-2023). Patients included were under 18 years old with an Injury Severity Score (ISS) over 12. We defined prolonged ED-LOS as more than 4 h. We analyzed demographic, clinical, institutional, and temporal variables. Multivariable logistic regression identified independent predictors of prolonged ED-LOS. We included 874 pediatric patients, with a median ED-LOS of 227.5 min. Prolonged ED-LOS was independently associated with treatment in teaching hospitals (OR 2.25, 95% CI 1.43-3.55), absence of trauma team activation (OR 2.08, 95% CI 1.35-3.22), and non-local nationality (OR 1.66, 95% CI 1.12-2.45). Prolonged ED-LOS was also linked to specific injury mechanisms: road traffic collisions (OR 13.89, 95% CI 1.75-110.00) and low-height falls (OR 13.87, 95% CI 1.68-114.73). Higher injury severity was associated with a decreased likelihood of prolonged ED-LOS (OR 0.94, 95% CI 0.92-0.96). The model showed acceptable discrimination (AUC 0.733). Prolonged ED-LOS in severely injured pediatric patients was primarily associated with system-level factors, specifically trauma team activation and hospital characteristics. Additionally, injury mechanisms and demographic factors contributed to prolonged ED-LOS. Optimizing trauma activation protocols and workflow processes, particularly in teaching hospitals, may reduce ED-LOS and improve the efficiency of pediatric trauma care.

articles.title: Temporal Patterns of Sexual Assault Presentations in U.S. Emergency Departments: Implications for Staffing and Forensic Readiness.
articles.abstract: Sexual assault (SA) remains a major public health issue, yet only a fraction of survivors seeks acute medical care in emergency departments (EDs). Although previous studies describe demographic disparities among SA survivors, national patterns of ED arrival timing and their operational implications for emergency care systems remain poorly characterized. To characterize the demographic and temporal patterns of ED presentations for SA in the United States. We conducted a repeated cross-sectional study using the Epic Cosmos database, including U.S. ED encounters related to SA from January 1, 2016 through December 31, 2024. Demographic characteristics and arrival patterns were compared with those of all other ED visits using odds ratios (ORs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Temporal distributions by day of week and 6-h arrival intervals were analyzed using chi-square testing and standardized Pearson residuals. Among 391,352,267 ED visits, 245,475 (0.06%) involved SA evaluation. Patients presenting with SA were disproportionately adolescents and young adults, female, Medicaid-insured, and from minoritized racial groups. Overnight arrivals (00:00-05:59) had significantly higher odds of SA presentation (OR, 1.45; 95% CI, 1.43-1.47), with peak presentations occurring on Sundays and Saturdays overnight. Morning presentations were consistently below expected levels. In 2016, 16% of patients presenting with SA arrived by ambulance; by 2024, this number had increased to 18%. SA presentations revealed distinct demographic and temporal patterns with important operational implications for EDs. Young and socially vulnerable populations are disproportionately affected. The concentration of presentations during overnight weekend hours highlights the need for expanded access to trauma-informed forensic services, including SA Nurse Examiner coverage and prehospital education, especially during high-demand periods.

articles.title: Comparative preclinical evaluation of an investigational topical hemostatic formulation against an active commercial comparator in rat arterial, venous and liver bleeding models under normal and heparinized conditions.
articles.abstract: An ideal topical hemostatic agent should provide rapid hemostasis, maintain clot stability after manipulation, and preserve a clean operative field. These requirements become particularly relevant under anticoagulated conditions and across different bleeding anatomies. To evaluate the preclinical performance of a topical hemostatic agent compared with a commercial comparator and saline control in standardized rat arterial, venous, and liver bleeding models under normal and heparinized conditions. A total of 144 adult male Wistar albino rats were allocated to 18 groups (n = 8 per group). Standardized abdominal aortic, vena cava, and liver bleeding models were established under normal and heparinized conditions. Vascular injuries were created with a 21 G needle and liver injury with a standardized 6 mm × 5 mm incision. Treatment was followed by a standardized 3-minute compression protocol. The primary endpoint was time to hemostasis. Liver blood loss was assessed gravimetrically. Rebleeding tendency and operative field quality were evaluated qualitatively. One-way ANOVA demonstrated overall between-group differences in time to hemostasis in all model-condition combinations (all P < 0.001). Across all anatomical models and coagulation settings, the investigational hemostatic agent consistently showed the shortest mean time to hemostasis, whereas saline-treated controls showed the longest times. Pairwise post hoc comparisons showed significantly shorter time-to-hemostasis values for the investigational agent than for the commercial comparator in four of the six model-condition comparisons; in the remaining two comparisons, the mean time-to-hemostasis values were numerically lower but not statistically significant. In the liver model, mean blood loss was numerically lowest in the investigational groups under both normal and heparinized conditions, although between-group differences were not statistically significant. Descriptive qualitative observations suggested cleaner operative fields and less post-manipulation rebleeding in the investigational groups. In this standardized multi-model rat study, the investigational topical hemostatic agent showed consistently shorter mean time-to-hemostasis values across arterial, venous, and liver bleeding models under both normal and heparinized conditions. Liver blood loss was numerically lower in the investigational groups, but the between-group differences were not statistically significant. These findings support further confirmatory preclinical evaluation.

articles.title: Effect of a stabilized liquid ozone-containing formulation delivered through a hyaluronic acid/poly-D,L-lactide scaffold on early osteochondral repair in a rat model.
articles.abstract: Articular cartilage has limited intrinsic repair capacity, and osteochondral defects may progress to degenerative joint disease. Ozone has anti-inflammatory properties but is highly reactive and short-lived in gaseous form. This study evaluated whether a stabilized liquid ozone-containing formulation delivered through a hyaluronic acid/poly-D,L-lactide (HA/PDL) scaffold improves early histological repair of osteochondral defects. Forty female Sprague-Dawley rats were randomly allocated to four groups (n = 10 each): healthy reference, untreated defect, HA/PDL scaffold, and HA/PDL scaffold impregnated with the stabilized liquid ozone-containing formulation. A 1-mm-diameter, 3-mm-deep osteochondral defect was created in the right femoral intercondylar region. Animals were euthanized on postoperative day 45. Histological repair was evaluated using the Modified Mankin score (0-14), and residual cartilage damage area was quantified in mm² on the index haematoxylin and eosin (H&E)-stained section using calibrated ImageJ analysis. All animals completed the study. Because the healthy reference group received zero scores for all histological variables, inferential analyses were restricted to the operated groups. Total Modified Mankin scores differed significantly among groups (p = 0.001), with the ozone-loaded scaffold group demonstrating lower scores than both the untreated defect group (p = 0.002) and the scaffold-only group (p = 0.006), whereas no difference was observed between the latter two groups (p = 1.000). Significant group differences were also observed for structure (p = 0.001) and tidemark integrity (p = 0.004). Residual cartilage damage area differed among the operated groups (p = 0.001) and was smaller in the ozone-loaded scaffold group than in the untreated defect group (p < 0.001), whereas the comparison with the scaffold-only group did not reach statistical significance (p = 0.169). The stabilized liquid ozone-containing formulation delivered through an HA/PDL scaffold was associated with improved early histological repair compared with untreated defects and yielded lower histological degeneration scores than scaffold implantation alone. Because the formulation comprised multiple components and no ozone-free vehicle control was included, these findings cannot be attributed specifically to ozone and should be interpreted as evidence of improved early histological repair rather than true cartilage regeneration. Not applicable (Experimental animal study).

articles.title: Fixation-specific modeling of age-frailty interactions to predict early mortality after hip fracture surgery.
articles.abstract: Early mortality after hip fracture surgery remains high. Existing risk models treat age and frailty as independent predictors and may not reflect how physiologic reserve modifies risk across fixation strategies. We evaluated whether modeling age-frailty interactions improves estimation of 30-day mortality. A retrospective cohort study using the American College of Surgeons National Surgical Quality Improvement Program (ACS-NSQIP) database (2019-2023) included adults undergoing intramedullary nailing (IMN), hemiarthroplasty, or plate fixation for femoral neck, pertrochanteric, or subtrochanteric fractures. Frailty was measured using a validated 5-item modified frailty index. Generalized additive models with bivariate spline surfaces generated procedure-specific mortality risk estimates. Secondary outcomes were assessed using propensity score-matched cohorts. Among 115,643 patients, 30-day mortality was 5.25%. Predicted mortality varied across age-frailty combinations, ranging from 1.41% to 28.83% for IMN, 1.26%-32.06% for hemiarthroplasty, and 0.48%-20.37% for plate fixation. IMN showed higher transfusion rates, while hemiarthroplasty demonstrated higher cardiopulmonary complication rates. Length of stay did not differ between procedures. Modeling age and frailty as interacting variables produces procedure-specific mortality risk estimates after hip fracture surgery. These estimates support patient counseling and perioperative decision-making using routinely available clinical data.

articles.title: Muscle or Subcutaneous Fat? A Prospective Ultrasonographic Study of Dorsogluteal Injection Accuracy in the Emergency Department.
articles.abstract: Dorsogluteal intramuscular (i.m.) injection is commonly used in emergency departments, but successful delivery into muscle tissue may vary depending on patient anatomy. This study aimed to evaluate the accuracy of dorsogluteal i.m. injections performed in the emergency department using immediate postinjection ultrasonography and to identify factors associated with successful i.m. deposition. This prospective observational study was conducted in the dedicated injection area of a tertiary care emergency department between June 1 and June 15, 2018. Adult patients receiving dorsogluteal i.m. injections were consecutively enrolled. After exclusions, 134 patients were included in the study. The primary outcome was ultrasonographic determination of whether the injectate was deposited in the i.m. or subcutaneous (s.c.) plane. To address interobserver reliability, 20 additional consecutive patients receiving injections underwent independent ultrasonographic assessment by both radiologists, each blinded to the other radiologist's classification. Agreement was summarized using overall percentage agreement and Cohen's κ with a 95% confidence interval (CI), where estimable. Of the 134 patients, 72 (53.7%) were men. Ultrasonography reported that 82 injections (61.2%) reached the i.m. plane, whereas 52 (38.8%) remained in the s.c. tissue. Successful i.m. deposition was significantly more frequent in men than in women (88.9% vs. 29.0%, p < 0.001). s.c. tissue thickness and combined skin-plus-s.c. tissue thickness reported stronger discrimination for s.c. deposition than body mass index (BMI). In the additional 20-patient dual-ultrasound reliability cohort, the radiologists agreed on the clinically dichotomized injection outcome (correct i.m. vs. incorrect s.c./s.c.-i.m. deposition) in 19 of 20 examinations (95.0%), with a Cohen's κ of 0.875 (95% CI, 0.638-1.000), indicating almost perfect agreement. A considerable proportion of dorsogluteal injections performed in the emergency department do not reach the target muscle tissue. Direct regional s.c. tissue thickness seems to be a more clinically informative determinant of injection success than BMI alone.

articles.title: The Benefit of Early Advanced Airway Management Depends on Prehospital Epinephrine Timing in Out-of-Hospital Cardiac Arrest: A Nationwide Cohort Study.
articles.abstract: The combined effect of epinephrine and advanced airway management (AAM) timing on out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA) outcomes remains poorly characterized. To investigate the interaction between epinephrine and AAM timing and their joint association with neurological and survival outcomes in OHCA. This retrospective study used Korea OHCA Registry data (August 2019-December 2023). We included adults receiving prehospital epinephrine and AAM. Epinephrine timing was early (=10 min) or late (>10 min) from emergency medical services arrival; AAM timing was early (=6 min) or late (>6 min). This yielded four groups: early epinephrine/early AAM (EE-EA), early epinephrine/late AAM (EE-LA), late epinephrine/early AAM (LE-EA), and late epinephrine/late AAM (LE-LA). Multivariable logistic regression and interaction analyses were performed for good neurological recovery (Cerebral Performance Category 1-2), survival to discharge, and prehospital return of spontaneous circulation. Of 20,662 eligible patients, 37.1% were in the EE-EA group. Compared with LE-LA, the EE-EA group had significantly higher odds of good neurological recovery (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] 2.44, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.93-3.08) and survival to discharge (aOR 2.18, 95% CI 1.87-2.55). The LE-EA group showed no significant benefit over LE-LA (aOR 0.99, 95% CI 0.71-1.40). A significant interaction between early epinephrine and early AAM was observed for neurological recovery (aOR 1.45, 95% CI 1.08-1.95; p=0.045). Early epinephrine combined with early AAM was associated with optimal neurological recovery. However, this multiplicative interaction was attenuated in sensitivity analyses addressing resuscitation time bias, suggesting a hypothesis-generating rather than confirmatory association.

articles.title: Fluoroscopy-assisted percutaneous management of posterior pelvic ring injuries via multiple transsacral and iliosacral screws in the supine position.
articles.abstract: When patients are positioned supine for percutaneous screw insertion to achieve posterior pelvic ring fixation, the edge of the operating table can impede screw insertion trajectories, thereby increasing the risk of cortical perforation, especially during iliosacral screw (ISS) placement. Multiple screw insertion might also potentially increase the risk of cortical perforation. The aim of this study was to evaluate the feasibility, safety, and efficacy of inserting multiple (≥2) transsacral screw (TSS) and ISS in the supine position via the application of specific surgical strategies and techniques developed in our institution. Patients who underwent stabilization of posterior pelvic ring injuries via percutaneous insertion of multiple TSS and/or ISS in the supine position between May 2018 and December 2025 were included in this study. Distinct screw insertion combination patterns at different vertebral levels, which were primarily determined by the variable anterior-posterior width of the transverse osseous pathway at the first sacrum, were employed for posterior pelvic ring fixation. Wound infection and neurovascular complications associated with screws insertion procedure were recorded. Postoperative CT scans were performed to assess the position of the screws. At follow-up, radiographic evaluations were performed to evaluate the complications including screw loosening, screw breakage, and non-union. A total of 149 large-diameter (≥7 mm) screws, including 123 TSSs and 26 ISSs, were inserted in a total of 69 consecutive patients. No wound infection and neurovascular complication associated with the screw insertion procedure were found postoperatively. Postoperative CT imaging demonstrated that all inserted screws were intraosseous. All patients were followed for an average of 19.5 months (range, 6.6-38 months). Only one screw (S2 TSS) breakage was noted, and no screw loosening and no bone nonunion occurred. Fluoroscopy-assisted percutaneous multiple large-diameter screws (TSS and ISS) insertion for posterior pelvic ring injuries with the patient positioned supine has been confirmed to be a feasible, safe, and effective surgical procedure.

articles.title: CCBE1 promotes wound healing in diabetic rats by improving the functional impairment of AD-MSCs induced by AGEs.
articles.abstract: The etiology of chronic and non-healing diabetic wounds is manifold; the progression of the non-healing phenotype is strongly associated with poor vascular networks. Mesenchymal stem cells (MSCs) are reckoned as a promising therapy for wound healing, especially in angiogenesis. Here, we explored the role of CCBE1 in diabetic wound healing using human adipose-derived MSCs (hAD-MSCs). Human adipose-derived hAD-MSCs were isolated and expanded through serial in vitro passaging. Cell proliferation and migration were evaluated using Cell Counting Kit-8 (CCK8) and scratch wound assays, respectively. collagen, and calcium-binding EGF domain-containing protein 1 (CCBE1) and vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) expression were analyzed via western blotting. Functional studies of CCBE1 were conducted using siRNA-mediated knockdown and plasmid-driven overexpression approaches. Type 2 diabetes mellitus was induced in Sprague-Dawley rats through a high-fat/high-glucose diet combined with streptozotocin administration. Full-thickness excisional wounds were generated on the dorsal skin, and the effects of CCBE1 modulation in hAD-MSCs on wound closure were examined. Reepithelialization and angiogenesis were analyzed using histological and immunohistochemical methods. Protein levels of CCBE1 and vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) were quantified by western blotting. hAD-MSCs showed a gradual decrease in cell proliferation, migrationand increased apoptosis, during advanced glycation end products (AGEs) conditions; meanwhile, CCBE1 and VEGF expression decreased The downregulation of CCBE1 inhibited cell proliferation and migration, and enhanced apoptosis, while CCBE1 overexpression enhanced proliferation and migration, and reduced apoptosis. Compared with untransduced hAD-MSCs, local subcutaneous injection of CCBE1-overexpressing hAD-MSCs accelerated wound closure, enhanced angiogenesis and reepithelialization at the wound bed, and increased VEGF levels in wound tissues. CCBE1 overexpression promoted hAD-MSC proliferation and migration and reduced cell apoptosis in vitro and accelerated diabetic wound closure, reepithelialization, and angiogenesis by improving hAD-MSCs in vivo. These beneficial effects of CCBE1 overexpression in diabetic wound healing by hAD-MSCs were at least partially mediated by increased VEGF levels in wound tissues.

articles.title: Corrigendum to "Is Our Understanding of Hyperosmolar Hyperglycemic State Accurate?" [The Journal of Emergency Medicine, Volume 79, December 2025, Pages 531-538].
MicroRNAs regulate viability, longevity and extracellular matrix secretions of mesenchymal stem cell-derived chondrocytes in vitro.
articles.abstract: Chondrogenic differentiation of human adipose tissue-derived mesenchymal stem cells (ADMSCs) is a promising strategy for cartilage regeneration, but its regulatory mechanisms remain incompletely understood. MicroRNAs (miRNAs) play critical roles in post-transcriptional control of lineage commitment and tissue development. This study aimed to identify miRNAs differentially expressed during ADMSCs chondrogenesis and explore their functional roles in chondrogenic gene regulation. ADMSCs were induced to undergo chondrogenic differentiation under defined conditions. miRNA expression profiles were analyzed, and significantly dysregulated miRNAs were identified. Bioinformatic and literature-based analyses were used to associate these miRNAs with chondrogenic transcription factors, signaling pathways, and cellular processes. Chondrogenesis was associated with distinct patterns of miRNA regulation. miR-140-5p, miR-520d-5p, miR-127-5p, and miR-218-5p were upregulated and correlated with increased expression of cartilage markers (SOX9, COL2A1, ACAN) and suppression of hypertrophy. These miRNAs were linked to TGF-β signaling, epigenetic regulation, and inhibition of terminal differentiation. Conversely, miR-145-5p, miR-101-3p, miR-194-5p, miR-199a-5p, miR-182-5p, miR-29a-5p, miR-20a-5p, miR-193b-5p, and miR-574-3p were downregulated, potentially relieving repression of transcription factors, signaling components, autophagy-related genes, and extracellular matrix regulators. Chondrogenic differentiation of ADMSCs is governed by coordinated miRNA regulation, involving activation of pro-chondrogenic miRNAs and suppression of inhibitory ones. This regulatory network integrates key molecular pathways required for stable cartilage formation and highlights potential targets for improving ADMSCs-based regenerative therapies.

articles.title: Factors associated with the occurrence and recurrence of road traffic injuries in car and motorcycle drivers: a cross-sectional study.
articles.abstract: To analyze the factors associated with the occurrence and recurrence of road traffic injuries (RTIs) in drivers. A cross-sectional study was conducted using a non-probabilistic sample recruited through virtual snowball sampling. Participants completed a questionnaire on the occurrence and recurrence of RTIs and their potential associated factors. Poisson multiple regression was used to identify factors associated with the lifetime occurrence and recurrence of RTIs, as well as their occurrence in the last 12 months. The lifetime prevalence of RTIs was 14.9% (95% confidence interval [95%CI]: 13.1-16.9), and the 12-month prevalence was 1.2% (95%CI: 0.8-1.6). The prevalence of recurrence (≥2 lifetime RTIs) was 5.1% (95%CI: 4.1-6.4). Higher prevalences were observed among male individuals (lifetime: adjusted prevalence ratio [APR]: 1.37, 95%CI: 1.07-1.76), individuals with low educational attainment (lifetime: APR: 1.94, 95%CI: 1.18-3.20; last 12 months: ≤8 years: APR: 3.31, 95%CI: 1.08-10.13; 9-11 years: APR: 4.47, 95%CI: 1.71-11.67), motorcyclists (lifetime: APR: 2.39, 95%CI: 1.96-2.92; last 12 months: APR: 5.44, 95%CI: 2.86-10.32), individuals aged 18-29 years (last 12 months: APR: 5.04, 95%CI: 1.92-13.27), individuals with a National Driver's License (lifetime: APR: 1.63, 95%CI: 1.02-2.60), and those who reported running red lights in the absence of surveillance cameras (lifetime: APR: 1.40, 95%CI: 1.09-1.80). Driving under the influence of alcohol (DUIA) was associated with RTI occurrence in both periods analyzed (lifetime: APR: 1.53; 95%CI: 1.15-2.05; last 12 months: APR: 3.45; 95%CI: 1.67-7.16) and with RTI recurrence (APR: 1.67; 95%CI: 1.00-2.78). Cell phone use to make and/or answer calls while driving was associated with RTI recurrence (APR: 2.62; 95%CI: 1.06-6.47). Being a motorcycle driver was also associated with RTI recurrence (APR: 4.98; 95%CI: 3.46-7.17). The occurrence and recurrence of RTIs were associated with sociodemographic and behavioral variables.

articles.title: "Wax on, Wax off".
articles.abstract: Mentors play a profound role in professional development, providing guidance, confidence, stability, and a sense of belonging. Yet the sudden loss of a mentor can leave a protégé untethered, especially when the relationship extends beyond professional guidance into the fabric of one's personal and professional identity. Drawing on the author's experience of unexpectedly losing a long-standing mentor, this reflection explores the grief and disorientation that can accompany the end of an important mentoring relationship. While painful, losing a mentor can reveal mentorship's lasting influence and prompt a transition from being mentored to becoming a mentor.

articles.title: Discharge to Street.
On Whether the Sickest Patient in the Emergency Department Is in the Waiting Room.
articles.abstract: One common maxim in clinical medicine is that the sickest patient in the emergency department may be in the waiting room (termed the waiting-room maxim). The purpose of this commentary is to discuss 5 pitfalls related to the waiting-room maxim that can sometimes transform a fundamentally smart idea into a popular misconception. Brevity makes a maxim powerful, yet also creates limitations by leaving out elaboration, logic, and evidence.

articles.title: Utility of Routine Testing in Asymptomatic Markedly Elevated Blood Pressure in the Emergency Department: A Prospective Cohort Study.
articles.abstract: Routine diagnostic testing for asymptomatic adults with markedly elevated blood pressure (BP) in the emergency department (ED) imposes a substantial operational burden despite uncertain clinical benefit. This study aimed to evaluate the prevalence and clinical significance of routine test abnormalities, identify predictors of actionable findings, and assess short-term clinical outcomes in this population. We conducted a prospective observational cohort study from May 2025 to February 2026. Asymptomatic adults (>18 years) with significantly elevated BP (systolic >180 mmHg or diastolic >110 mmHg) were enrolled. Acute target-organ damage (TOD) was ruled out using a structured symptom checklist. Primary outcomes were clinically meaningful test abnormalities and 7-day adverse clinical events. Among 210 enrolled patients (median presenting BP 199/118 mmHg), repeat measurement after >30 min showed a significant spontaneous median systolic reduction of 24 mmHg without acute intervention. While 13.3% of patients had clinically meaningful abnormalities, only 3.3% necessitated hospital admission and 3.3% required immediate treatment modification. Most abnormalities (10.9%) triggered process-driven outcomes, such as specialist consultations, without altering ED disposition. Chronic kidney disease (CKD) was the sole independent predictor of actionable findings (aOR = 8.28, (95% CI: 2.09-32.82; p = 0.003). The 7-day adverse event rate was low (1.9%), with no deaths or events occurring in patients without meaningful ED-based abnormalities. Routine screening for asymptomatic severe hypertension is low-yield and often identifies subacute conditions rather than emergencies. Validating 2025 American Heart Association (AHA)/American College of Cardiology (ACC) guidelines, a risk-stratified approach prioritizing CKD screening and rapid outpatient follow-up ensures safety while optimizing emergency resources.

articles.title: N-acetyl cysteine (NAC) preconditioning enhances the efficacy of bone marrow derived mesenchymal stem cells for healing of skin burn wounds.
articles.abstract: Burn injuries are associated with excessive oxidative stress and inflammation that impair mesenchymal stem cell (MSC) survival and regenerative function. This study investigated whether N-acetylcysteine (NAC) preconditioning could enhance the therapeutic efficacy of bone marrow-derived MSCs (BMSCs) in oxidative stress conditions and burn wound healing. In vitro, BMSCs were preconditioned with NAC (5 or 10 mM) prior to H₂O₂ exposure, and cell viability, proliferation, oxidative stress markers, and regenerative gene and protein expression were evaluated. In vivo, BMSCs isolated from male Sprague Dawley rats were transplanted into second-degree thermal burn wounds induced in female rats, and wound healing was assessed over 21 days using macroscopic, histological, biochemical, and molecular analyses. NAC preconditioning significantly improved BMSC viability, proliferation, and morphology under oxidative stress while reducing LDH release. NAC-treated BMSCs exhibited increased antioxidant enzyme activities (SOD, CAT, and GSH), reduced malondialdehyde (MDA) levels, and enhanced expression of PCNA, SDF-1, CXCR4, VEGF-A, and IGF-1. In vivo, transplantation of NAC-preconditioned BMSCs accelerated wound contraction, improved re-epithelialization, increased hydroxyproline content, and promoted collagen deposition and tissue regeneration. Furthermore, NAC-preconditioned BMSCs enhanced antioxidant defenses and upregulated SDF-1, CXCR4, VEGF-A, and IGF-1 expression in wound tissues. Collectively, these findings demonstrate that NAC preconditioning enhances the survival, antioxidant capacity, paracrine activity, and regenerative potential of BMSCs, resulting in improved burn wound healing. NAC-preconditioned BMSCs may represent a promising strategy for stem cell-based treatment of burn injuries.

articles.title: Temporary internal stabilisation for staged reconstruction of critical long-bone defects: A biomechanical study.
articles.abstract: Critical long-bone defects remain a major challenge in orthopaedic trauma and reconstructive surgery, particularly following high-energy injury, infection, and extensive segmental bone loss. Their management frequently requires staged reconstruction with temporary skeletal stabilisation between initial debridement and definitive reconstruction. External fixation remains an established strategy during this interval, while temporary internal fixation represents an alternative approach. However, biomechanical evidence regarding purpose-designed modular intramedullary constructs used in conjunction with polymethylmethacrylate (PMMA) spacers remains limited. To evaluate the axial and bending mechanical characteristics of a modular intramedullary temporary stabilisation system used with a PMMA spacer and to compare its mechanical behaviour with selected plate and external fixation constructs in segmental long-bone defect models. Five synthetic long-bone models were evaluated, with one specimen assigned to each experimental configuration. Three 50-mm femoral defect models were stabilised using plate osteosynthesis, external fixation, or modular intramedullary temporary stabilisation. Two additional modular intramedullary configurations comprised a 400-mm femoral defect and a 50-mm humeral defect. Each specimen underwent sequential quasi-static axial compression and bending using a TIRATEST-2151 testing machine, with continuous force-displacement recording and complementary optical displacement assessment. Axial and bending stiffness were analysed descriptively; no inferential statistical comparisons were performed. In the 50-mm femoral defect configurations, measured axial stiffness was approximately 60 N/mm for plate osteosynthesis, 80 N/mm for external fixation, and 90 N/mm for modular intramedullary stabilisation; corresponding bending stiffness values were approximately 1.0, 0.6, and 1.2 N/mm, respectively. The 400-mm femoral modular configuration demonstrated axial and bending stiffness of 155 and 1.2 N/mm, respectively, while the 50-mm humeral modular configuration showed the highest measured values, at 325 and 1.5 N/mm. Given the single-specimen design, these differences were analysed descriptively and no inferential comparisons were performed. The modular intramedullary temporary stabilisation system demonstrated measurable axial and bending stiffness across the tested segmental defect configurations, including the 400-mm femoral model. These findings provide an initial mechanical characterisation of the concept and support further replicated biomechanical evaluation incorporating standardised spacer preparation, additional comparators, and torsional and cyclic loading.

articles.title: Association of early hyperosmolar therapy and operative interventions in severe traumatic brain injury.
articles.abstract: Hyperosmolar therapy, hypertonic saline (HTS) or mannitol (MAN), is one of the standard management algorithms in Traumatic Brain Injury (TBI). There is a gap in information regarding the impact of the timing of starting the hyperosmolar therapy and outcomes. Our hypothesis was that early hyperosmolar therapy would reduce the operative interventions (craniotomy or craniectomy). The Trauma Quality Improvement Program (TQIP) database of 2019-2023 was queried for the study. Patients aged 18 years and older who suffered severe TBI, defined on Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS) score 8 or less and Abbreviated (brain) Injury Scale (AIS) score 3-5, who received HTS or MAN were included in the study. The propensity score matching method was used to compare the patients' characteristics and outcomes between the early (hyperosmolar therapy time of start ≤3 h after admission) and late groups (the therapy was started >3 h after admission). A total of 673 patients fulfilled the inclusion criteria. Propensity score matching resulted in 174 pairs of patients. There were no significant differences found between the early and late groups regarding the age in years (median [IQR]: 49.5 [ 30.5-70] vs 53.5 [ 35-66], P = 0.765), GCS (median [IQR]: 3 [3-6] vs. 3 [3-6], P = 0.718), Injury Severity Score (ISS) (median [IQR]: 25[17-26] vs. 25[17-26], P = 0.85), non-reactive pupils ( n (%): 28.7% vs. 28.7%) and significant midline shift ( 48.9% vs. 48.9%). The pair-matched analysis showed no significant difference between the early and late groups in operative interventions (13.8% vs. 20.1%, P = 0.161) and operative intervention within 24 h (10.3% vs. 17.8%, P = 0.67) or overall mortality (37.4% vs. 31.6%, P = 0.295). There was a significantly lower number of ICU days (median [IQR]: 6 [3-10] vs. 8 [3-14], P = 0.026), and ventilator days (median [IQR]: 4 [2-8] vs. 5 [2-12.8], P = 0.008) identified in the early group when compared to the late group, respectively. Starting hyperosmolar therapy within 3 h of hospital admission in severe TBI patients was not associated with any differences in operative interventions, overall mortality, but was associated with shorter ventilator days and intensive care (ICU) days.

articles.title: Renal Point-of-Care Ultrasound as a Screening Tool for Ureterolithiasis in Emergency Department Patients With Pyelonephritis.
articles.abstract: Pyelonephritis with concurrent ureterolithiasis is associated with substantial morbidity and mortality, yet data on using point-of-care ultrasound (POCUS) to evaluate these patients are limited. To evaluate the utility of hydronephrosis on POCUS to identify ureterolithiasis in patients with pyelonephritis. This retrospective study included patients 18 years or older presenting to a tertiary care emergency department (ED) between January 2015 and April 2025, diagnosed with pyelonephritis, who had a renal POCUS. Patients were excluded if they lacked flank pain or costovertebral angle tenderness, had no urinalysis, or had incomplete imaging data. The primary outcome was diagnostic performance metrics of hydronephrosis on POCUS for identifying ureterolithiasis in patients with pyelonephritis. Secondary analyses included urinalysis results, ED length of stay (LOS), time to imaging completion, and return ED visits within 2 weeks. Of 439 patients identified, 363 were included; 173 received POCUS alone, and 190 received both POCUS and computed tomography (CT). Ureterolithiasis was identified in 25 patients (6.9%). In the combined cohort, hydronephrosis on POCUS demonstrated 84.0% sensitivity and 85.2% specificity for ureterolithiasis, with a negative predictive value of 98.6%. Median LOS for discharged patients receiving POCUS alone was 135 min shorter than those receiving both POCUS and CT (241.5 vs. 376.5, p< 0.0001). In this retrospective cohort of ED patients with pyelonephritis who underwent renal POCUS, absence of hydronephrosis on renal POCUS was associated with a lack of concurrent ureterolithiasis. Renal POCUS alone had a shorter ED LOS; however, further studies are needed to determine the efficacy and safety of a POCUS-guided approach.

articles.title: Validation of Diagnostic Scoring Systems in Patients With Clinical Suspicion of Necrotizing Soft Tissue Infection: A Cohort Study.
articles.abstract: Several scoring systems have been developed and are used to aid in the differentiation of necrotizing soft tissue infection (NSTI) from non-necrotizing soft tissue infections; however, their diagnostic performance in patients with clinical suspicion of NSTI requiring surgical evaluation remains uncertain. To validate the diagnostic performance of commonly used scoring systems in patients presenting with clinical suspicion of NSTI and requiring surgical evaluation. We conducted a retrospective cohort study at a tertiary referral center from September 2018 to December 2022. Adult patients presenting to the emergency department with clinical suspicion of NSTI and subsequent surgical consultation were included. The diagnostic performance of Laboratory Risk Indicator for Necrotizing Fasciitis (LRINEC), modified LRINEC (MLRINEC), Japanese LRINEC (J-LRINEC), and SIARI (Site other than lower limb, Immunosuppression, Age, Renal impairment, and Inflammatory markers) scores was evaluated. A total of 359 patients were included, including 214 with NSTI and 145 with non-necrotizing soft tissue infections. Patients with NSTI had significantly higher LRINEC, MLRINEC, and J-LRINEC scores than those without NSTI (all p < 0.001). However, substantial overlap in score distributions was observed between groups. The areas under the curve (AUCs) were 0.663 for LRINEC, 0.693 for MLRINEC, 0.720 for J-LRINEC, and 0.486 for SIARI. Although higher score thresholds demonstrated relatively high specificity, sensitivity remained suboptimal across all evaluated scoring systems. Although several scoring systems demonstrated statistically significant differences between groups, substantial overlap remained between NSTI and severe non-necrotizing SSTIs, indicating that these scores should not be used as standalone diagnostic tools.

articles.title: Predictive Value of the Hemorrhage After Thrombolysis Score for Tissue Plasminogen Activator-Related Intracranial Hemorrhage: Emergency Department Cohort Study.
articles.abstract: Intravenous tissue plasminogen activator (tPA) improves outcomes in acute ischemic stroke but carries a risk of intracranial hemorrhage, particularly parenchymal hematoma (PH), which is associated with poor prognosis. Early risk stratification remains clinically important. To evaluate the diagnostic performance of the Hemorrhage After Thrombolysis (HAT) score in predicting PH following intravenous tPA in the emergency department. This secondary analysis included a single-center retrospective cohort conducted between October 2023 and February 2025. Adult patients with acute ischemic stroke treated with intravenous tPA within 4.5 h were included. Baseline clinical, laboratory, and imaging data were collected. The primary outcome was PH on 24-h cranial computed tomography. Diagnostic performance was assessed using receiver operating characteristic analysis, with the optimal cutoff determined by the Youden index. A total of 120 patients were included (mean age 70.2 ± 13 years; 57.5% male). PH developed in 11 patients (9.17%). HAT scores were significantly higher in the PH group (p < 0.001). The HAT score showed good discriminative performance for PH (area under the curve [AUC]: 0.871), with an optimal cutoff of 1 (sensitivity 82.6%, specificity 90.9%). For overall hemorrhagic transformation, performance was also good (AUC: 0.786). PH was associated with increased mortality and morbidity. The HAT score demonstrates good diagnostic performance for predicting PH after thrombolysis. It may serve as a practical tool for risk stratification and post-treatment monitoring in the emergency department.

articles.title: Disease burden of spinal fractures attributable to road injuries among working-age population in China during 1990-2023: An analysis based on the global burden of disease 2023.
articles.abstract: Spinal fractures attributable to road traffic injuries impose a substantial disease burden on the working-age population. Nevertheless, the current affairs in the disease burden of spinal fractures among this demographic in China have not been systematically investigated. To evaluate the disease burden of spinal fractures and their subtypes attributable to road traffic injuries among the working-age population (15-69 years) in China from 1990 to 2023, and to forecast variation tendency through 2040. Leveraging data from the GBD 2023, data on the incidence rate, YLDs count, ASIR, and ASYR of spinal fractures and their subtypes triggered by road traffic injuries among China's working-age population during 1990-2023 were extracted. Joinpoint regression analysis and age-period-cohort models were employed to investigate trajectories in disease burden. The Bayesian age-period-cohort model was applied to project the disease burden from 2024 to 2040. From 1990-2023, the incidence and YLDs counts of spinal fractures triggered by road injuries among China's working-age population elevated by 26.24% and 53.30%, respectively.
