Clinical outcomes were evaluated according to the Ratliff classification. Fracture union was achieved in 95.1% of patients. Initial displacement and reduction quality were significantly associated with both clinical outcomes and complication rates (p<0.05). Delayed surgery was linked to a higher incidence of AVN (p=0.013). Physeal penetration was associated with worse clinical outcomes, especially an increased risk of PPC (p=0.002) and AVN (p=0.031). Pediatric femoral neck fractures remain associated with high complication rates. Initial displacement, inappropriate reduction, prolonged time to surgery, and physeal penetration were found to be risk factors for complications. Early anatomical reduction and physeal-sparing fixation are key to improving outcomes.

articles.title: Protective effects of pramipexole on testicular torsion and detorsion injury in rats.
articles.journal: Ulusal travma ve acil cerrahi dergisi = Turkish journal of trauma & emergency surgery : TJTES
articles.abstract: Testicular torsion induces ischemia-reperfusion injury, which is predominantly mediated by oxidative stress and inflammatory cascades. Pramipexole, a pharmacological agent widely used in neurological practice, possesses potent antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and anti-apoptotic properties. The aim of this experimental study was to evaluate the potential protective effects of pramipexole on testicular ischemia-reperfusion injury using a rat model of testicular torsion-detorsion, through both biochemical and histopathological analyses. A total of 18 male rats were randomly divided into three groups. Group 1 was designated as the control group. In Group 2, only a testicular torsion-detorsion model was established to evaluate testicular ischemia-reperfusion injury. In Group 3, a similar torsion-detorsion model was created. In addition, rats in this group received intraperitoneal pramipexole (0.5 mg/kg) immediately after testicular detorsion. The aim was to assess the effects of pramipexole on testicular ischemia-reperfusion injury. At the end of the experiment, blood samples were collected for biochemical analyses, and orchiectomy was performed for histopathological evaluation of testicular tissues. Biochemical analyses showed that malondialdehyde (MDA) levels were significantly increased in Group 2 compared with the other groups (p<0.001). Similarly, tumor necrosis factor-alpha and interleukin-1beta levels were significantly higher in Group 2 than in the other groups (p<0.001). In Group 3, both pro-inflammatory cytokine levels and MDA levels were significantly reduced compared with Group 2 (p<0.001). Furthermore, glutathione peroxidase and superoxide dismutase activities were significantly increased in Group 3 compared with Group 2 (p=0.002 and p<0.001, respectively). Histopathological evaluation revealed a significant improvement in all testicular damage scores, including vasocongestion, inflammation, and edema, in Group 3 compared with Group 2 (p<0.001). Likewise, the mean Johnsen score in Group 3 was calculated as 8.37±0.62, which was significantly higher than that observed in Group 2 (p<0.001). Pramipexole appears to be an effective pharmacological agent in alleviating the effects of testicular ischemia-reperfusion injury.

articles.title: Short-segment fixation including the fractured vertebra versus long-segment fixation in thoracolumbar fractures a ≥10-year comparative study.
articles.journal: Ulusal travma ve acil cerrahi dergisi = Turkish journal of trauma & emergency surgery : TJTES
articles.abstract: The aim is to compare the long-term clinical and radiological outcomes of posterior long-segment fixation (LS) versus short-segment fixation (SSIF) involving the fractured vertebra in patients with thoracolumbar fractures, based on a follow-up period of at least 10 years. Patients who underwent surgical treatment for thoracolumbar fractures between 2002 and 2013 were retrospectively reviewed. Neurologically intact patients with a AO Spine thoracolumbar fractures classification system A2, A3, and A4 and a minimum follow-up of 10 years were included in the study. Exclusion criteria included osteoporotic, pathological, multilevel fractures, and prior thoracolumbar surgery. Forty-six patients met the inclusion criteria (LS fixation, n=22; SSIF İncluding The Fractured vertebra, n=24). All procedures were performed at a single center by the same senior spine surgeon. Clinical outcomes were assessed using the Oswestry disability ındex (ODI) and visual analog scale (VAS). Radiological evaluation included Sagittal Cobb Angle (SCA) and anterior central vertebral body height (ACVBH). Complications and revision surgeries were recorded. Operative time was shorter in the SSIF group than in the LS group (138±8 minutes vs. 149±9 min; p<0,001, p<0.05 for both) and post-operative hospital stay was shorter in the SSIF group than LS group (4.3±1.2 days vs. 5.0±1.1 days; p=0.045, p<0.05 for both). Both groups showed post-operative improvement in ODI (p=0.312), VAS (p=0.083), SCA (p=0.418), and ACVBH (p=0.421), with no statistically significant between-group differences at final follow-up ODI (p=0.496), VAS (p=0.597), SCA (p=0.694), and ACVBH (p=0.512) (p>0.05 for all). No statistically significant differences were observed between groups in implant-related complications, junctional pathology, or revision surgery rates (p>0.05 for all). SSIF including the fractured vertebra yields long-term clinical and radiological outcomes comparable to those of LS fixation in thoracolumbar fractures. In suitable patients, this approach is a reliable surgical option for a shorter instrumented segment and a more mobile vertebral segment.

articles.title: Traumatic diaphragmatic injuries from the perspective of thoracic and general surgery: analysis of patient management using the Injury Severity Score (ISS) and Modified Shock Index (MSI).
articles.journal: Ulusal travma ve acil cerrahi dergisi = Turkish journal of trauma & emergency surgery : TJTES
articles.abstract: Traumatic diaphragmatic injury (TDI) is a rare but severe clinical condition associated with high mortality following blunt or penetrating thoracoabdominal trauma. Due to concomitant injuries, the diagnosis of traumatic diaphragmatic injury remains challenging and may be easily overlooked. This study aimed to evaluate the diagnosis and surgical management of traumatic diaphragmatic injuries through a retrospective analysis conducted at a single center between 2016 and 2024. Data from 41 patients who underwent surgical treatment for TDI between 2016 and 2024 were analyzed. Patients were classified into three groups according to the diagnostic process: those diagnosed intraoperatively without prior imaging (Group 1), those who underwent imaging but were diagnosed intraoperatively (Group 2), and those diagnosed preoperatively by computed tomography (CT) (Group 3). Demographic characteristics, mechanisms of injury, surgical approaches, postoperative complications, and prognostic scores, including the Injury Severity Score (ISS) and Modified Shock Index (MSI), were evaluated. Most patients were male (97.6%), and the left hemidiaphragm was the most frequently injured side (63.4%). Penetrating trauma (68.2%) was more common than blunt trauma, with gunshot wounds (34.1%) and stab wounds (34.1%) representing the most common mechanisms of injury. Laparotomy was the most frequently performed surgical approach (41.5%), and primary repair was achieved in 92.5% of patients. The overall postoperative complication rate was 37.5%, with atelectasis being the most common complication (26.7%). ISS scores were significantly higher in patients diagnosed intraoperatively than in those diagnosed preoperatively by imaging (p<0.001). Patients who underwent surgery within the first two hours after admission had higher ISS scores than those who underwent delayed surgery (p<0.001). ISS scores were significantly higher among patients operated on by the General Surgery department than among those treated by the Thoracic Surgery department. In contrast, MSI scores were lower in Thoracic Surgery patients who underwent emergency surgery for hemothorax than in General Surgery patients. TDI remains a diagnostically challenging condition, and early surgical intervention is crucial for reducing mortality. Despite advances in imaging techniques, some cases continue to be overlooked because of concomitant injuries. Therefore, a high index of clinical suspicion and close patient monitoring are essential for timely diagnosis. Furthermore, differences in ISS and MSI scores between patients managed by different surgical specialties may reflect variations in trauma severity, surgical decision-making, and timing of intervention.

articles.title: Hepatectomy is associated with favorable long-term outcomes related to septic complications in patients with localized hepatolithiasis.
articles.journal: Ulusal travma ve acil cerrahi dergisi = Turkish journal of trauma & emergency surgery : TJTES
articles.abstract: Hepatolithiasis can lead to the development of severe complications such as liver abscesses, secondary biliary cirrhosis, and intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma. While major liver resection is under debate, conservative approaches may not be curative. In this report, long-term results of surgical treatment were presented. A retrospective analysis of patients who underwent surgical treatment for hepatolithiasis between September 1999 and August 2020 was conducted. Clinical symptoms, stone distribution, interventions, complications, residual and recurrent stone rates, and long-term outcomes were evaluated. Fifty-two patients were identified. Twenty-eight were female, and 24 were male, with a mean age of 50 years (range: 22-75 years). Thirty-two patients had localized disease; 13 had stones in the right hepatic lobe and 19 in the left. Twenty patients had bilateral stones. In the localized disease group, patients underwent either liver resection (n=20) or conservative surgery (hepaticojejunostomy or T-tube drainage following stone clearance, n=12). In the bilateral disease group, only conservative surgical approaches were employed. The overall post-operative complication rate was 46%, and was higher after conservative surgery (p<0.26). However, bile leakage occurred more frequently following resection (15% vs. 6%). There was no mortality, and median post-operative hospital stay was 12 days (range: 5-55). Recurrence occurred in 5 patients (10%) during a mean follow-up period of 134 months (range; 25-275); all in the conservative treatment group, except one. Four patients developed hepaticojejunostomy strictures, whereas portal vein thrombosis and secondary biliary cirrhosis occurred in two patients each. Thirteen patients (25%) died during follow-up; two deaths were directly related to the disease. Ten-year disease-free survival was significantly better after resection compared to conservative surgery (85% vs 58%, p<0.05). Liver resection offers superior outcomes compared to conservative surgery in patients with localized intrahepatic stones. However, in patients with bilateral involvement, treatment needs to be individualized.

articles.title: Emergency department evaluation of injuries caused by falls from horses: A retrospective study.
articles.journal: Ulusal travma ve acil cerrahi dergisi = Turkish journal of trauma & emergency surgery : TJTES
articles.abstract: Since their domestication, horses have played an important role in human life. Today, horseback riding is widely practiced for recreational and therapeutic purposes. Despite this, horseback riding-related injuries remain an underreported public health problem in the emergency medicine literature. The aim of this study was to evaluate the injury patterns, management strategies, and clinical outcomes of patients presenting to the emergency department after falls from horses. This retrospective study included patients who presented to the emergency department of Sancaktepe Martry Prof. Dr. Ilhan Varank Education and Research Hospital between 2019 and 2024 following falls from horses. Patient data were obtained from the hospital information system and Picture Archiving and Communication System. Demographic characteristics, injury location, treatment modality, length of hospital stay, and clinical outcomes were recorded and analyzed statistically. A total of 86 patients were included in the study, of whom 43 (50%) were male and 43 (50%) were female. The mean age was 34±12.1 years (range: 7-69 years). Eight patients (9.3%) were under 18 years of age, while 78 patients (90.7%) were adults. Eighteen patients (20.9%) required hospital admission, whereas 68 patients (79.1%) were managed on an outpatient basis in the emergency department. Injury severity was assessed using the Injury Severity Score, with a mean value of 7.6. The majority of patients had minor injuries. The most commonly injured body region was the upper extremity, observed in 39 patients (45.3%). Surgical intervention was required in 18 patients (20.9%). Pelvic and spinal injuries were significantly more common among female riders, whereas lower extremity injuries predominated among male riders (p<0.05). Five patients (5.8%) required post-operative intensive care. One patient with severe head trauma (Glasgow Coma Scale 5) who was not using protective equipment died during follow-up. Horseback riding-related injuries frequently involve multiple organ systems and may present to the emergency department with varying levels of severity. Although many patients sustain high-energy trauma, most are managed within the scope of orthopedic and traumatology services, with a considerable proportion requiring surgical or conservative intervention. This study represents the first comprehensive evaluation in Turkey of patients presenting to the emergency department after falls from horses. Given the potential risk of severe injury and mortality, the absence of protective equipment in the fatal case suggests a possible role of safety measures; however, further studies are needed to better define their impact.

articles.title: Clinical findings of thoracic injuries in forensic trauma and their importance in medico-legal evaluation.
articles.journal: Ulusal travma ve acil cerrahi dergisi = Turkish journal of trauma & emergency surgery : TJTES
articles.abstract: Trauma remains one of the leading causes of mortality worldwide. Thoracic injuries constitute a frequently encountered group of injuries, particularly among young adult trauma patients. This study aimed to examine thoracic trauma of forensic relevance from a medico-legal perspective and to determine the demographic characteristics, clinical findings, and the relationship of these findings with forensic reporting. A total of 254 patients presenting with traumatic thoracic injuries to a secondary care hospital between 2023 and 2025 were retrospectively analyzed. The patients' age, sex, origin of the incident, clinical characteristics, and medico-legal outcomes were evaluated. Of the cases, 75.2% were male, and the mean age was 48 years. Blunt trauma accounted for 86.2% of injuries, with in-vehicle road traffic accidents representing the most common cause (49.2%). According to current Turkish medico-legal guidelines, all cases were classified as injuries that could not be treated with simple medical intervention; 83.1% involved bone fractures, and 79.9% were considered life-threatening. Rib fractures were identified in 70.5% of cases, whereas intrathoracic injuries were detected in 71.3%. The most frequently observed pathologies were pneumothorax (70.2%) and hemothorax (50.8%). The frequencies of pneumothorax and hemothorax were significantly increased in cases of assault-related injury (p<0.05), whereas parenchymal contusion was more frequently observed in accidental injuries. The mortality rate was 6.7%. Although thoracic trauma is relatively uncommon in secondary healthcare institutions, it carries a high risk of life-threatening complications and the potential for complex medico-legal consequences. Standardized and detailed medical documentation is essential to ensure consistency in legal processes and criminal sanctions. Focusing medico-legal evaluations not only on the trauma mechanism but also on anatomical injury and associated complications may improve the standardization and objectivity of forensic reports.

articles.title: Suicide and accidental deaths in railway incidents: A 10-year retrospective regional autopsy study.
articles.journal: Ulusal travma ve acil cerrahi dergisi = Turkish journal of trauma & emergency surgery : TJTES
articles.abstract: Railway-related deaths represent an important public health issue, emphasizing the value of preventive strategies. This study aimed to provide a regional perspective on railway-related fatalities in Ankara to contribute to the development and imple-mentation of preventive measures by evaluating crime scene findings and autopsy reports. A retrospective review was conducted of autopsies performed at Ankara Group Chairmanship, The Council of Forensic Medicine between 2015 and 2024. Among 67 cases in which death occurred at a train station or railway, 48 traumatic railway-related deaths were included in the study. For each case, demographic and incident-related variables were collected, including age, sex, date of incident, location, manner of death, type of incident, type of railway transport, and specific scene characteristics. Comparative analyses were performed according to manner of death and type of incident. The majority of railway-related fatalities were suicides. Both suicide and accident cases were predominantly male; suicide cases were most frequent in the 30-39 age group, whereas accident cases were most frequent in the 40-49 age group. Temporal analysis showed that suicides peaked in autumn and during the 12: 00-17: 59 time interval, whereas accidental deaths were most frequent in winter and during the 06: 00-11: 59 interval. Nearly all suicides took place in subway stations. Compared with accidents, suicide victims were younger and more frequently sustained skull fractures, spinal injuries, and dismemberment, whereas sternum fractures and liver injuries were more common in accidents. These findings highlight differences in injury patterns between suicide and accident cases, together with a marked concentration of suicide deaths in subway settings. Preventive and regulatory measures may help reduce railway-related fatalities, including both accidents and suicides. Public awareness campaigns, installation of physical barriers, and the integration of automated video-based early warning systems may play a key role in decreasing subway suicides. From a forensic medicine perspective, the distinct injury patterns may have practical implications for forensic interpretation, particularly in cases with limited scene information.

articles.title: Diagnostic accuracy of oblique radiographic views for ulnar-sided carpometacarpal dislocations: A cadaveric study.
articles.journal: Ulusal travma ve acil cerrahi dergisi = Turkish journal of trauma & emergency surgery : TJTES
articles.abstract: Dislocations and fracture-dislocations of the ulnar-sided carpometacarpal (CMC) joints are rare injuries that are often overlooked during initial clinical evaluations, primarily due to subtle radiographic findings and overlapping anatomical structures. Missed or delayed diagnosis can result in chronic instability, persistent pain, and suboptimal functional outcomes. This study aimed to assess and compare the diagnostic sensitivity and specificity of different oblique radiographic projections in identifying fifth CMC joint dislocations using a controlled cadaveric model. Six human cadaveric hands, preserved with the modified Larssen solution, were used in this study. Oblique fluoroscopic images were acquired at 30°, 45°, and 60° angles from the lateral view, under three different joint conditions: Native alignment, 25% dislocation, and 50% dislocation of the fifth CMC joint. Standardized imaging was performed using a fixed digital setup. A total of 54 randomized images were included in a questionnaire reviewed by 20 orthopedic surgeons (7 consultants and 13 senior registrars), who classified the fifth CMC joint status as 'dislocated,' 'not dislocated,' or 'uncertain.' Sensitivity, specificity, and overall diagnostic accuracy were calculated for each oblique angle. The 60° oblique radiographs exhibited the highest sensitivity for identifying dislocations but had a moderate reduction in specificity. In contrast, the 30° view showed the highest specificity but the lowest sensitivity. The 45° oblique radiographs provided a more balanced diagnostic profile. Overall, the 60° oblique radiographs achieved the greatest diagnostic accuracy. Interestingly, senior registrars demonstrated significantly higher diagnostic accuracy than consultants. While the 60° oblique radiographs showed the best performance in detecting fifth CMC dislocations, their sen-sitivity was not sufficient for use as a standalone diagnostic tool. When clinical suspicion persists despite inconclusive radiographs, computed tomography scan is recommended.

articles.title: The association between Vitamin D metabolites and low-energy distal radius fractures in non-elderly adults.
articles.journal: Ulusal travma ve acil cerrahi dergisi = Turkish journal of trauma & emergency surgery : TJTES
articles.abstract: This study aimed to evaluate Vitamin D metabolism in non-elderly adults with low-energy distal radius fractures (DRFs). Serum 25-hydroxyvitamin D [25-(OH)D] and 1,25-dihydroxyvitamin D [1,25-(OH)D] levels were compared with those of age- and sex-comparable healthy controls. In addition, the relationship between Vitamin D metabolites, other biochemical parameters, and articular involvement patterns was investigated in patients with low-energy DRFs. This observational case-control study included 102 patients aged 18-60 years with low-energy DRFs and 138 age- and sex-comparable healthy controls in the same age range. Serum 25-(OH)D and 1,25-(OH)D levels were compared between the fracture and control groups. In the fracture group, Frykman fracture type was used to assess articular involvement, and its relationship with alkaline phosphatase (ALP), calcium (Ca), phosphate (P), parathyroid hormone, and Vitamin D metabolite levels was analyzed. A total of 240 participants were included in the final analysis. Age and sex distribution were similar between the fracture and control groups (p=0.285 and p=0.855, respectively). Serum 25-(OH)D levels did not differ significantly between groups (p=0.557), whereas serum 1,25-(OH)D levels were significantly lower in the low-energy DRF group than in controls (p<0.001). Among Frykman fracture subgroups, significant differences were found in 25-(OH)D, ALP, and Ca levels (p=0.009, p=0.001, and p=0.002, respectively). Extra-articular fractures were associated with lower 25-(OH)D and higher ALP levels compared with other fracture subgroups, while Ca levels were lower than in selected intra-articular fracture subgroups. Non-elderly adults with low-energy DRFs had lower serum 1,25-(OH)D levels despite having serum 25-(OH)D levels comparable to those of healthy controls. These findings suggest that alterations in active Vitamin D metabolism may be associated with low-energy DRFs in this population. Assessment of active Vitamin D metabolites together with conventional biochemical parame-ters may provide a more comprehensive understanding of the metabolic profile of non-elderly adults presenting with low-energy DRFs.
